summary: Analyze the v7 StarNet sim and produce a build plan to turn it into a real gamified AI-agent harness desktop app

maps.subsystem: Rendering & World (canvas renderer, tile/room map, character sprites, movement + work-loop state machine)
maps.purpose: A vanilla-JS 2D canvas engine that draws a tilted-top-down pixel-art space station: a baked static environment (floors/walls/hull/lighting) plus live actors (agents, furniture screens, parcels) y-sorted and re-drawn every frame under a baked lightmap. A separate WORLD module runs a tile-grid pathfinding + plan-sequencer state machine that makes each pixel character walk to a location, sit, and enter a "working" posture. This subsystem is exactly the visual + movement substrate the new harness needs for "agent walks around a room, walks to a placed object, sits and works."
howItWorks: COORDINATE SYSTEMS: three layers. (1) Tile grid: COLS=78 x ROWS=55, TILE=12px (map.js:8). (2) World pixels: tileX*12; map.js exposes W=COLS*TILE=936, H=ROWS*TILE+14=674 (the +14 leaves room for the extruded south hull face). (3) Screen: the canvas is a single fixed-resolution buffer (cv.width=W, cv.height=H in render.js:882) CSS-stretched to fit; render.js:876 toLocal() converts mouse events back via (clientX-rect.left)*(W/rect.width). A body stores px/py in world pixels AND tile{x,y}; foot anchor convention is px = tileX*T + T/2, py = tileY*T + T-1 (agents.js:67,630).

THERE IS NO SCROLLING CAMERA. The whole station fits in one 936x674 buffer and is scaled by CSS (index.html canvas#station). 'Camera' = the CSS scale of that fixed buffer. Panning/zoom would have to be added (drawImage offset or ctx.translate/scale) — none exists today.

PER-FRAME RENDER LOOP (render.js:787 frame(tMs), called from main.js:102 inside requestAnimationFrame after SIM.tick + WORLD.tick): (a) fill space black + draw 230 scrolling parallax stars; (b) lazily buildBase() once, then ctx.drawImage(baseCv) — the entire static environment is a prebaked offscreen canvas; (c) drawExteriorAnim() for blinking dish/nav LEDs/engine glow; (d) build a y-sort list of {y, draw} for all furniture, parcels, and agent bodies, sort ascending by y, draw in order (render.js:806-839) — this is the painter's-algorithm depth sort; (e) ctx.drawImage(lightCv) over everything (baked darkness with light carved out); (f) drawGlows/drawLabels/drawHazards/drawPropHover and floating +$ text and hover name tags.

BAKING (render.js:107 buildBase): all static geometry is rendered ONCE into baseCv (an offscreen canvas the size of the world): hull plate + seams + rivets, per-room and per-corridor procedural floors (bakeRoomFloor/bakeCorridorFloor), edge ambient occlusion, door thresholds, walls (bakeWalls draws n-faces tall and s/w/e as wall-tops to sell the tilt), additive room lighting pools, rounded-corner (chamfer) arc walls, and a downward hull extrusion (bakeHullExtrusion stamps the silhouette down to fake 3D side walls). Re-baked only if baseCv is null. THIS IS WHY USER-PLACED OBJECTS ARE HARD TODAY (see simulatedParts).

LIGHTMAP (render.js:280 buildLightMap -> lightCv): a full-screen dark overlay (rgba(10,8,4,0.62)) painted over rooms/corridors, then light is CARVED BACK with globalCompositeOperation='destination-out' radial gradients at room centers, lamp positions (lampPos[]), doorways, and windows, plus a source-over vignette. Drawn over the WHOLE scene each frame so agents/furniture sit in the same light. A few lamps (flickers[]) get a live additive shimmer in drawGlows().

TILE/ROOM/ZONE MODEL (map.js): zones{} maps a zoneId to an inclusive tile rect {x1,y1,x2,y2}. ROOM_IDS lists the 10 real rooms; everything else (hub, spines, corridors) is a corridor. zoneGrid[idx(x,y)] = zoneId per tile; blocked[] = Uint8Array of impassable tiles; sitTiles{} = 'x,y'->true for seats. allRects[] drives all bake loops. roomAt(tx,ty) returns roomId or 'corridor'. A 'room' is therefore just a labeled rectangle of tiles plus baked decoration — there is no Room object/class.

WALKABILITY + PATHFINDING (map.js): walkable(x,y) = in-bounds AND zoneGrid!=null AND !blocked. canStep enforces zone boundaries except through doorSet (built from doorDefs pairs). path(sx,sy,tx,ty) is a plain BFS over 4-neighbors returning an array of {x,y} tiles (map.js:358). propAt(tx,ty) and pwGrid give tile->interactive-furniture lookup for hover/click (also checks one tile south for sprite overhang).

AGENT BODY + WALK/SIT/WORK STATE MACHINE (agents.js WORLD): bodies{id} each have px,py,tile,path[],state('work'|'walk'|'idle'|'social'),sitting,working,dir,phase,plan. tick(dt,t) (agents.js:616): if path non-empty, move px/py toward path[0] at 42*pace px/s, set dir from dominant axis, snap tile on arrival, shift path, call arrive() when empty. goTo(b,tx,ty) computes a BFS path and sets state='walk',sitting=false. arrive() sets posture by goal: at the home station tile it sets state='work',sitting=true,dir='north' (desks face away from camera). working = (state==='work' && hasTask) is set in think() (agents.js:471). So the entire 'walk to your computer, sit, work' loop ALREADY EXISTS — goTo a station tile, arrive sits you, a task flips working=true.

PLAN SEQUENCER (agents.js:190 runPlan): plans are step arrays of {go:{x,y}}|{face}|{sit}|{wait}|{do:fn}. This is a clean, reusable scripting layer for 'walk here, face this, sit, do X' — onDeliverable/planBriefing/planVisit/planProp are all built on it. This is the ideal hook for 'user places a computer -> agent walks to it and sits'.

CHARACTER RENDERING: TWO renderers. (1) IMAGE-BASED (assets.js SPRITES.drawBody, the real path when sprites loaded): loads a PixelLab sprite manifest (assets/sprites/manifest.json), keys like 'minion.walk.south' -> [Image] frames; per-agent recolor via CSS hue-rotate filter (filterFor) baked into a cached tinted canvas; downscaled (minion 2/3, ultron 0.85). drawBody picks an animation track from b.state: walk->'walk' @10fps, working->'type'/'sit' facing north @6fps, sitting->'sit'/'rot', else idle 'rot' with a sine bob; frame index = floor(now/(1000/fps)+phase)%len; foot-anchored at (px,py). (2) PROCEDURAL FALLBACK (sprites.js:3622 drawProcedural): hand-draws a ~14px-tall pixel body with 2-frame leg walk cycle (step=floor(now/140)%2), sitting shrinks height to 11, working blinks the arms (typing), robot visor, headset antenna, beer can, plus overlays (alert !, speech bubble, selection box). drawAgent (sprites.js:3579) tries SPRITES first, else procedural.

FURNITURE RENDERING (sprites.js): F{} is a dispatch table of ~50+ procedural pixel-art draw functions (desk, desk2, pixelrig, holotable, beltH, djbooth, etc.). drawFurn(f,work) computes pixel rect from f.x/f.y/f.w/f.h and calls F[f.t](X,Y,W,H,f); screens only light when f.work is true (render.js detects an agent working within +/-2 tiles and passes work=true). Helpers box/inset/bevel/glow/scanl/blink build the CRT look. now is injected via SPR.setNow each frame; SPR.setCtx lets portrait/UI code borrow the context.
maps.realLogic: Genuinely reusable, non-faked engineering: (1) The whole tile/grid/zone model + walkable/canStep/BFS path in map.js is real, self-contained game logic with no sim dependency. (2) The movement integrator in WORLD.tick (px/py lerp toward path tiles, dir derivation, arrival snapping) and goTo/arrive are real and exactly model 'walk to a tile and sit'. (3) The plan sequencer (runPlan with go/face/sit/wait/do steps) is a clean reusable behavior-scripting engine. (4) The render loop's y-sort painter's algorithm, the bake-once-then-blit pattern, and the destination-out lightmap are solid, performant canvas techniques. (5) assets.js sprite loading + per-agent hue-rotate recolor + animation-track picking is real and directly supports per-user custom avatars. (6) The procedural furniture/agent art in sprites.js is real pixel art generation that runs with zero assets. (7) util.js (hash, shade, money, event bus, mini-synth SFX) is dependency-free.
maps.simulatedParts: What is set-dressing / must change for the real harness: (1) The 'work' signal is FAKE — f.work / b.working is driven by SIM having a taskId; the lit monitor, typing arms, and CRT animations are pure cosmetics with NO connection to a real model call. For the new app, b.working must be driven by a real agent actually running (an in-flight model/tool call), and the screen content should reflect real output. (2) ALL geometry and furniture are HARD-CODED at module-load: zones{}, chamfers, doorDefs, the 200-line furniture[] array, and stations{} are literals in map.js, and the entire environment is BAKED into baseCv once. There is no runtime API to add/move/remove a room, a wall, a tile, or a piece of furniture — placing an object at runtime would require rebuilding zoneGrid/blocked/sitTiles/pwGrid AND re-running buildBase()+buildLightMap(). (3) The 17 agents, their personalities (PERS), buddies, social spots, belts, parcels, and the elaborate deliverable/briefing/inspection journeys are authored fiction tied to the fake economy. (4) Floating '+$' sale text, P&L tickers, hazards, party-mode disco lighting are economy theater. (5) No camera/scroll/zoom and a single fixed 936x674 buffer — fine for a fixed station, but a user-built room of arbitrary size needs a real camera.

rebuildForRealHarness: A DATA-DRIVEN, MUTABLE WORLD MODEL: replace the hard-coded zones/furniture/stations literals with runtime state (e.g. a room descriptor + an objects[] array the user edits). Provide addObject/removeObject/moveObject that incrementally update zoneGrid, blocked, sitTiles, and pwGrid instead of relying on module-load construction.

INCREMENTAL / LAYERED BAKING: today buildBase() paints the entire environment into one canvas once. For user placement, either (a) re-bake on each edit (cheap enough — it's one pass and only happens on placement, not per-frame), or (b) split into a static floor/wall bake + a dynamic object layer drawn per-frame in the y-sort. Same for buildLightMap() (lamp/window light must update when objects move).

OBJECT-DEFINES-A-WORKSEAT SYSTEM: generalize stations{} so a user-placed 'computer' object registers a sit tile + a facing + a 'work anchor'. Then reuse goTo(seatTile)+arrive() so the agent walks over and sits. Add an object schema {type, tile, w, h, sit?, workAnchor?, sprite}.

REAL 'working' DRIVER: wire b.working/f.work to an actual agent run state (model request in flight / tool call executing) instead of SIM.taskId, so the seated-at-computer animation is the true visual of real work. The lit-screen cosmetic stays; only its trigger changes.

A CAMERA: add pan/zoom (ctx.setTransform or a camera offset applied before drawing world layers, with inverse applied in toLocal hit-testing) so an arbitrary-sized user room can be larger than the viewport.
PLACEMENT/EDIT UI: a build mode (ghost preview on the tile grid, validity check via walkable + footprint-free, snap to TILE) — none exists today; render.js only does hover/select, not placement.

ASSET PIPELINE for PixelLab avatars/objects: a manifest + tint cache like assets.js, but generated per-user at runtime (the PixelLab MCP can create the character/tileset frames; feed them through the existing tintFrames/drawBody path).

RENDER.init(canvas, clickCb) (render.js:880; wired in main.js:113): the click callback already routes agent-click -> open agent panel and prop-click -> open terminal. This is where 'click agent -> show real live cost/usage' and 'click object' hooks attach.
The plan-step {do: fn} hook (agents.js:209): arbitrary code runs at a point in a walk sequence — ideal to kick off a real task when an agent reaches a placed computer, and {wait}/onDone to end it.

keyFiles.role: Canvas world renderer: per-frame loop frame(), one-time environment bake buildBase(), destination-out lightmap buildLightMap(), y-sort actor draw, exterior/glow/label passes, mouse hit-testing + hover/click in init()/toLocal(). No scroll camera (fixed 936x674 buffer).

World geometry + logic: TILE/COLS/ROWS, zones/rooms as tile rects, chamfers/doors/windows, zoneGrid/blocked/sitTiles/pwGrid, walkable/canStep, BFS path(), roomAt/propAt/randomSpotIn. ALL furniture + stations are hard-coded literals here (the thing to make runtime-mutable).

WORLD module: agent bodies, the walk/sit/work state machine, path-follow integrator in tick(), goTo/arrive posture logic, and the {go/face/sit/wait/do} plan sequencer (runPlan) that scripts 'walk to X, sit, work'. The exact loop the user wants, minus a real work trigger.

SPRITES: PixelLab image-sprite loader + per-agent hue-rotate recolor (tintFrames/filterFor) + drawBody() that maps body state (walk/sit/type/idle) to animation tracks and frame timing. The real character-animation path and the avatar-customization seam.

SPR: ~50+ procedural pixel-art furniture draw fns in F{} (desk/desk2/pixelrig = 'computer' objects), plus procedural agent fallback drawProcedural() (walk cycle, sit, typing arms) and shared drawOverlays(). 3674 lines, mostly furniture art; screens light only when f.work.
Dependency-free helpers: hash, shade, clamp/lerp, money formatting, the U.bus pub/sub event bus used across render/agents/sim, and a tiny WebAudio SFX synth. Safe to reuse wholesale.

Boot + requestAnimationFrame loop wiring: calls SIM.tick -> WORLD.tick(dt,t) -> RENDER.frame(t); RENDER.init click callback routes agent/prop clicks to UI. The orchestration seam where the fake SIM gets swapped for the real agent runtime.

risks: Runtime object placement fights the bake-once design: the entire environment (floors/walls/hull/lighting) is precomputed into baseCv/lightCv and only built when null. Any placed/moved object needs zoneGrid/blocked/sitTiles/pwGrid updates AND a re-bake (or a new dynamic layer). Re-baking the whole 936x674 canvas per placement is acceptable (it's not per-frame) but must be wired deliberately — there is no invalidate/rebuild API today.

No camera/scroll/zoom: a user-built room larger than the fixed buffer will not fit. Adding a camera touches both rendering (transform before world layers) and input (toLocal must invert the transform) — easy to get half-done and break hit-testing.

Coordinate coupling: agents anchor at py = tileY*T + T-1 and the lightmap/extrusion assume the fixed layout (e.g. H gets +14 for the south hull). Changing TILE size or world bounds ripples through bake math, AO depths, wall heights, and shadow offsets.

Walkability vs furniture footprint: blocked/sitTiles/pwGrid are built once at module load from the literal furniture[]. Placing an object without updating all three desyncs collision, seating, and click-targeting (e.g. agents walking through a new object, or no sit tile registered).
'working' is cosmetic and tied to SIM.taskId; if SIM is removed without re-pointing b.working/f.work, all seated-at-computer screen animation goes dark even when a real agent is running.

sprites.js is huge (3674 lines) and entirely station-themed; reusing it wholesale imports a lot of bespoke art. Cherry-pick the helpers + the few object types you need (desk/pixelrig/agent) rather than dragging in the full economy-specific catalog.

PixelLab sprite path assumes a static manifest.json fetched at init; per-user runtime avatar generation needs an async pipeline (generate -> load -> tint) and a graceful procedural fallback while frames are missing (the drawAgent SPRITES.ready check already provides this pattern).

maps.purpose: The deterministic-ish game engine that drives the colony: a per-game-minute "heartbeat" advances a single global state object S, spawns tasks for 17 agents, walks each task through a research -> production -> publishing -> sales pipeline, and books revenue/cost into an economy. Every agent "doing work," every deliverable's quality, every token cost, and every sale is invented locally with Math.random() and content pools — there are no model calls, no tool calls, and no money. This is the exact subsystem that must be replaced (or wrapped) so that real model invocations, real tool calls, and real metered cost stand in for the faked numbers.
howItWorks: HEARTBEAT: main.js loop() (line 94) runs on requestAnimationFrame. It accumulates real wall-time into simAcc at settings.speed, and every time 1000ms of sim-time elapse it calls SIM.tick(mins) (capped at 30 mins/frame). SIM.tick (sim.js:814) just loops minuteTick() N times. So one game-minute == one logical sim step; default 1 game-min per real second.

GLOBAL STATE S: created by newState() (sim.js:9-38). Single mutable object holding: time (minutes since day1 07:00), mode (MANUAL/AUTO), party timer, rev {total,etsy,fiverr,other}, costs, station level/xp, agents map, tasks[], feedback[], notifs/ops/chat logs, listings counts, insights counts (research inventory), saasProjects[], mrr, pivots map, fiverrRating, history[], dayAcc accumulators, kindStats telemetry, shipQueue[]. Per-agent record (sim.js:12): skill, morale, autonomy, reliability, xp, level, tasksDone, earned, spent, fbApproved/Denied, taskId, statusTxt.

MINUTE TICK (sim.js:681): S.time++, then for each agent: if idle, pull the next 'todo' task for that agent and mark it 'active'; if working, advance t.prog by a computed speed and call completeTask when prog>=dur. Then morale drifts toward 62. Then generators() spawns new work, salesTick() rolls sales, the shipQueue fallback flushes overdue publishes, the ultronQueue flushes delayed chat lines, AUTO-mode autopilot resolves stale feedback, and on minute boundaries pivotCheck/checkMilestones (every 60) and dayRollover (every 1440) fire.

TASK SPAWN: generators() (sim.js:412) is the pipeline source. Each agent has a genReady(id, cooldown) gate (sim.js:401) that fires on a randomized cooldown, plus agentFree() (sim.js:406). NOVA/CURIE emit 'research' tasks that increment S.insights[store]. Factory agents (FORGE/VECTOR/PROMETHEUS) consume an insight (S.insights[store]--) to emit apparel/candle/custom tasks. PIXEL/ATLAS/QUILL/CIPHER/VYBES emit fiverr/assets/article/saas/song tasks on their own cadence. So 'research -> production' is literally an integer inventory counter (insights) being incremented by researchers and decremented by factories.

TASK PROGRESS (the FAKE WORK timer): minuteTick line 695 computes sp = speedMult() * (0.7 + skill/180) * (morale<40?0.75:1) * (partyOn?0.5:1) and does t.prog += sp until t.prog >= t.dur. dur is a random integer (e.g. U.irnd(40,70)) set at task creation. This loop IS the 'agent working on the computer' — purely a counter racing a random target, no work performed.

COMPLETION & QUALITY (FAKE QUALITY): completeTask (sim.js:174) books cost via taskCost(), then invents quality via rollQuality() (sim.js:160): q = 32 + skill*0.55 + (morale-60)*0.18 + U.rnd(-13,13) + perkBonus, with retry/note/rush/low-morale modifiers, clamped 15-99. If quality < flagBelow(agent) for FLAGGABLE kinds (or a commander flag is set), the task goes to 'review' and a fake self-doubt feedback entry is created; otherwise finalize() runs.

FINALIZE & PIPELINE BRANCH (sim.js:212): bumps agent xp/level/skill, station xp, kindStats. Then a switch on t.kind: 'research' increments S.insights (feeds production); production kinds (apparel/candle/custom/assets/song/article) push a 'ship' onto S.shipQueue to be hand-carried to HERALD; 'publish' increments S.listings (feeds sales) and kindStats.shipped; 'fiverr' books revenue immediately via earn(); 'saas' advances a 3-stage build then sets proj.mrr; 'pivot' sets a 2-day store boost. This switch is the publishing stage and the join between production and sales.

PUBLISHING HAND-CARRY: finalize pushes {id, agentId, room, kind, payloadQ, flavor, due} to S.shipQueue (sim.js:253). WORLD walks the sprite to HERALD and calls SIM.heraldHandoff(shipId) (sim.js:326), which creates a 'publish' task for HERALD. minuteTick (sim.js:710) has a fallback: any ship past its 'due' is force-handed-off so a reload/party never loses a publish.

SALES (FAKE REVENUE): salesTick (sim.js:359) runs every minute. For each Etsy store it computes a per-minute sale probability p = min(L,14)*0.00040 * (skill/60) * saleMult() * pivotBoost where L = S.listings[key], and on U.chance(p) books amt = U.rnd(rev[0],rev[1]) * revMult() via earn(). Assets/articles/songs have their own probability lines. Revenue is conjured from listing counts and dice — no buyers, no transactions.

ECONOMY / COST MODEL (FAKE COST): two cost sources. (1) Per-task: taskCost(agentId) (sim.js:155) = U.rnd(model.costMin, model.costMax) * costMult(), where model is DATA.MODELS[agent.model] with hardcoded costMin/costMax per model (FABLE 1.40-3.10, OPUS 0.80-2.10, GPT 0.14-0.42 in data.js:7-11). Added to S.costs and ag.spent on every completeTask. (2) Daily subscription burn: dayRollover (sim.js:752) sums DATA.DAILY_SUBS[model] across all agents (FABLE 9.00, OPUS 7.50, GPT 4.20/day, data.js:12) * costMult() into S.costs. Net = S.rev.total - S.costs. These are the only two places 'token cost' exists, both pure RNG/constants.

FEEDBACK-DRIVEN STAT GROWTH: feedback(fbId, verdict, note, opts) (sim.js:514). Commander verdicts (approve/deny/retry/archive) adjust the agent's morale/skill/autonomy and grant station xp. A non-empty note gives an extra skill/autonomy bump (sim.js:524). approve finalizes the held task with a +4 quality bump; deny/archive fail it; retry spawns a discounted retry task. agentNote() and praise/scold via chat also nudge skill/morale/autonomy. So 'training' is numeric stat deltas that feed back into rollQuality and the progress speed formula.

ULTRON BRAIN (intent routing, faked NLU): playerMessage(raw) (sim.js:585) lowercases the text and regex-matches against INTENTS[] (sim.js:566) to pick an agent+kind and spawn a playerOrder task, plus party/status/help/praise/scold special cases. Replies are canned strings from DATA.C pools, delayed via queueUltron/queueChat into S.ultronQueue. No model is consulted.

PERSISTENCE/AUTOSAVE: main.js save() (line 16) writes localStorage['starnet_save_v1'] = {sim: SIM.serialize(), settings}. SIM.serialize() (sim.js:826) = JSON.stringify({S, idc:U._id}); SIM.load() (sim.js:827) parses and re-inits from saved S. Autosave runs on setInterval(save, 30000) and on beforeunload (main.js:123-124). reset() removes the key and reloads. Whole game state is one JSON blob in localStorage.
maps.realLogic: Genuinely reusable, non-faked engineering: (1) The pipeline ARCHITECTURE — a producer/consumer inventory model (research increments S.insights, production consumes it, publishing increments S.listings, sales consume that) is a real, sound design that a real harness can keep. (2) The task lifecycle state machine: todo -> active -> (review) -> done/failed, with per-agent single-slot scheduling, a queue, prioritize/rush/flag controls, and a review/approval gate. (3) The event bus (U.bus pub/sub) decoupling sim from UI/world — every meaningful state change emits an event (task, sale, stats, feedback, deliverable, level, day). (4) Persistence/serialization scaffolding (single-blob JSON save/load with lazy migration via KS() and the `if(!S.kindStats)` guards). (5) The XP/level/perk/milestone/objective progression system and the kindStats telemetry aggregation. (6) The hand-carry shipQueue with an idempotent, reload-safe fallback timer — a robust pattern for 'async work that must not be lost'. (7) The feedback->stat->future-output loop is a real reinforcement structure (just driven by fake quality today). All of this is engine plumbing that survives the transition; only the value SOURCES (work output, quality, cost, sales) are fake.
maps.simulatedParts: EVERYTHING that represents the result of work or the price of work is faked and must become real: (1) WORK EXECUTION — t.prog += sp racing a random t.dur (minuteTick ~line 695) is a stopwatch, not work; no deliverable artifact is ever produced, only a flavor string picked from DATA.C pools. (2) DELIVERABLE CONTENT — titles/flavors come from DATA.C.apparel/candles/petstyles/fiverr/assets/articles/saas/songs/research; no image, file, article, or app is generated. (3) QUALITY — rollQuality() (sim.js:160) is dice over agent stats; there is no evaluation of any real output. (4) TOKEN COST — taskCost() (sim.js:155) = U.rnd(model.costMin,model.costMax); DATA.MODELS cost ranges and DATA.DAILY_SUBS (data.js:7-12) are invented constants; no tokens are counted. (5) TOOL CALLS — the named tools (GPT-IMAGES-2, Printify, Fiverr webhook, PixelLab, Suno, Medium, YouTube) appear only as ops()/chat() log strings and agent role text; none are invoked. (6) REVENUE/SALES — salesTick() (sim.js:359) and the fiverr/saas/mrr payouts in finalize() mint money from listing counts * probability * U.rnd ranges; there are no buyers, marketplaces, or payments. howItWorks: BODY MODEL (mkBody, lines 62-75): each agent is one plain object keyed by id in `bodies{}`. Fields split into POSITION (px/py = float pixel coords, tile = integer grid coords, path = array of remaining tile waypoints), POSTURE/ANIM (state ∈ work|walk|idle|social, sitting bool, working bool, dir ∈ north/east/south/west, hasCan, alert), EXPRESSION (bubble {until,txt}, glance {dir,until}, act = human-readable status string surfaced to the UI), and CONTROL (plan, meet, goal, timers: breakUntil/nextWander/nextFidget/glanceCd/meetCd/phase). Initial state is seated at desk (state:'work', sitting:true).

IDLE FSM (think, lines 465-545): called probabilistically from tick (~3% per body per frame). Priority ladder: (1) party mode forces everyone except ULTRON to a leisure spot; (2) if b.plan exists, return — the sequencer owns the body; (3) if mid hallway-meet, return; (4) if social break expired, walk home; (5) if currently walking, return; (6) ULTRON inspection cadence; (7) if hasTask -> go sit at desk and work; (8) else idle behaviors gated by nextWander timer and a single Math.random() roll: alert->pace by desk; roll<0.20 visit buddy; <0.20+0.28*social -> pool or leisureTrip; <0.62 -> prop or random spot in own room; else -> return to desk. Personality table PERS (lines 18-36) scales pace, restlessness, sociability, preferred hangout, buddy, and chat frequency per agent.

PLAN SEQUENCER (runPlan, lines 190-220): the heart of 'purposeful movement'. A plan is {tag, steps[], i, flush?, onDone?}. Step types: {go:{x,y}} (issues a path via MAP.path, sets state='walk', waits for arrival, aborts if knocked off course), {face:dir}, {sit:bool}, {wait:ms} (non-blocking timer), {do:fn} (side effect — set act string, emit parcel, trigger chat/bubbles/glances). runPlan loops synchronously through instantaneous steps and returns when it hits a blocking step (walking or waiting). On completion sets goal='work', clears act, runs onDone (usually homeDone). abortPlan (222-228) bails and runs an optional flush() that guarantees the sim side-effect still happens even if the walk was interrupted.

INTENTIONAL JOURNEYS (built as plans, lines 237-462, each wired to a bus event in init): onDeliverable = stand up -> carry to belt -> drop parcel -> watch it ride (wait 2400) -> walk to HERALD in publishing -> brief him (handoff fires, both get bubbles/glances/banter) -> walk home. planBridgeVisit = present flagged work to ULTRON. planBriefing = carry research intel to a builder's desk. planVisit = idle buddy visit. planProp = walk to room focus prop and ponder. planPool = claim pool table + recruit a partner for the far end, alternate shots. planInspection = ULTRON visits the busiest working room. leisureTrip = quarters break to a reserved social spot.

PATHFINDING: WORLD does not implement the search itself — it delegates to MAP.path(x0,y0,x1,y1) (called in goTo line 157 and the {go} step line 198). MAP.path returns an array of tile waypoints (empty array = already there, null = unreachable). WORLD consumes that array in tick: it lerps px/py toward path[0] at `42 * pace * moraleSlow * dt` px/s (line 628), snaps to the tile and shifts the waypoint on arrival, and derives `dir` from the dominant axis of motion (lines 633-634). Arrival (no waypoints left) calls arrive(b) which decides final posture by b.goal.

RESERVATION / OCCUPANCY: props and social spots are claimed by simple ownership flags, no formal lock manager. Social spots: leisureTrip (448-462) filters MAP.social by a `taken` predicate that checks whether any other body's socialSpot matches the x/y, picks a free one, and assigns b.socialSpot (the reservation). Pool table: a module-level `poolBusyUntil` timestamp gates planPool, and POOL_SPOTS (line 52) is a fixed 2-element list claimed for ~24s. free() (line 78) = MAP.walkable AND not a sit tile, used by standNearTile/standNearFurn (83-96) to find an unoccupied adjacent stand position next to a desk or furniture piece.

AWARENESS / 'ALIVE' LAYER (scanWorld, lines 548-613, throttled to ~4Hz): glances — seated agents turn their head toward nearby walkers, passing parcels (in factories), the bridge (when alert), or fidget while working. Hallway encounters — two walkers within ~17px stop, face each other, pop chat bubbles, optionally emit banter, and set cooldowns (pairCd per pair, meetCd per body). This is pure set-dressing that makes the room feel inhabited.

MAIN TICK (tick, lines 616-651): per body — resolve hallway-meet pause; run plan; advance along path (movement + dir + arrival); if stranded mid-walk resolve via arrive; else maybe think(). Then throttled scanWorld, then advance parcel cosmetics along belts. nowMs is the module clock set from the tMs argument.

howItWorks: CLICK -> WINDOW: A map click calls the RENDER.onClick callback registered in main.js (~line 113), which calls PROPTERM.open(propKey, pos). PROPTERM.open looks up DEFS[key] (a static table of ~30 window definitions keyed by prop id e.g. 'etsy1','fiverr','bridge_main'), and if not already open calls spawn(key,def,pos) then rerender(key). place() computes a viewport-clamped position (offset from the prop, or a cascade for blind opens); lastPos[key] remembers position across re-opens for the session.

WINDOW CHROME: spawn() builds a `.term.pw` div with a header (accent-colored title bar, a live headState() chip, roll-up '▁' and close '✕' buttons) and an empty `.pw-body`. Dragging is handled by a single set of module-level mousemove/mouseup listeners keyed on dragKey (leak-free; ui.js uses the same one-shared-listener pattern via termDrag). Double-click or the roll-up button toggles `.pw-rolled`; for game windows it calls ARCADE.pause()/resume(). z-order via U.zTop() on mousedown.

RENDER PIPELINE: rerender(key) sets a module-global `collect=[]`, calls def.build() to produce the body HTML, appends uplink(key,def) if the window is agent-backed, then stashes `w.feeds = collect` (the list of agent ids whose live feeds appeared in this window) and nulls collect. feedHTML()/nowPlaying() push their agId into collect as a side effect during build — so the window auto-discovers which feeds it must animate. scrollTop is preserved across rerenders. The whole body is re-built once per second by PROPTERM.tick() (called from UI.slowTick), EXCEPT windows that are being dragged, rolled up, game windows, or windows whose INPUT has focus (so a note being typed is never destroyed).

~7fps LIVE-FEED ENGINE: PROPTERM.open starts setInterval(fastTick, 140ms) (~7fps) when the first window opens; cleared when the last closes. fastTick() increments fastN, then for every unique agId across all open windows' `feeds` arrays it advances that agent's FEED[agId] state and patches the DOM by id (#fs-AGID stream, #fc-AGID canvas, #ft/#fm/#fx meters, #fcap caption, #fu uplink-ms) WITHOUT rebuilding HTML. This id-targeted patching is why the feed keeps streaming smoothly even while the 1/sec full rerender is suppressed.

STREAMING TERMINAL (the fake): FEED[agId] = {lines[], cur, target, pend, tok, lastTask}. Each tick, if no target line, nextLine(agId,t) picks the next line from weighted pools: ~30% a tool call ('▶ images.generate {...}' from TOOLS[kind]) which queues a paired response ('◀ 200 OK (NNNms)') in st.pend; ~15% a reasoning beat ('… evaluating N directions' from THINK); otherwise a kind-specific verb line (VERBS[kind]+VERBS.generic) with {tok}/{ms}/{seed}/{flavor} placeholders filled by fill(). The target string is then revealed char-by-char (st.cur = target.slice(0, len + irnd(2,5))); on completion it is pushed to st.lines (capped at 9, shows last 7) and tok is incremented by irnd(9,70). streamHTML() renders the last 7 lines plus the current partial line with a blinking '█' cursor. Job transitions emit '—— dispatch accepted: WO ...' / '—— deliverable handed off' banners. Special agents (ULTRON/RELAY/LEDGER/RAVEN/HERALD) have custom gen() generators and alwaysOn:true so their consoles stream even with no task.

METERS (the fake): TOK = st.tok, a running counter incremented per tick (irnd(9,70) while working). COST = estCost() = model.costMin + (costMax-costMin)*pct/100 where pct is task progress percent — i.e. cost is interpolated from how far the fake task bar has moved, not from real usage. (2) The render discipline: build()-returns-HTML + scrollTop preservation + the suppress-rerender-while-input-focused guard + the id-targeted DOM patching in fastTick (so a high-rate stream coexists with a 1/sec full rebuild without thrashing or losing user input). (3) The `collect`/feeds auto-discovery mechanism: build() side-effect-registers which agent feeds a window contains, so the animator knows exactly what to drive. (4) The progressive ASCII canvas: getMask reveal-rank caching, the paint-in-by-percent renderer with a render-head, and the animated dashboards (matrix/net/graph/wave/cal) are real, performant procedural-graphics code. (5) The feedback/uplink interaction model (note drafts surviving rerenders, note-focus-aware refresh, two-step arm/confirm for destructive actions, transient flash confirmations) is solid UX scaffolding. (6) arcade.js is a complete, correct fixed-timestep canvas game with proper mount/unmount/pause/resume — the canonical pattern for embedding real interactive content in a window. All of this is presentation/interaction logic that is independent of where the data comes from."
maps.simulatedParts: "Everything that represents 'the agent doing work' is procedurally generated set-dressing, not real: (1) STREAMING TERMINAL LINES — nextLine() picks from hardcoded pools (VERBS, TOOLS, THINK, RESP, IDLE_LINES, per-agent gen() functions) and fill()s in random numbers via {tok}/{ms}/{seed}/{n1-4}; the char-by-char typing is just target.slice(0, len+irnd(2,5)). No model is invoked, no tool is called, the 'tool calls' like 'images.generate {model:\"gpt-images-2\"}' and their '200 OK (NNNms)' responses are strings. (2) TOKEN METER — st.tok is a local counter bumped by irnd(9,70) per tick. (4) CONTEXT METER — ctxPct() = 14 + pct*0.62, pure function of progress. (5) UPLINK LATENCY — uplinkMs() is a hash. consoleOrder refuses past 5 queued jobs as a UX nicety; with real agents the meaningful limits are concurrency, rate limits, and credit balance — the 5-job cap must be replaced by real backpressure or users will queue work that silently can't run.

Global module singletons (FEED, wins, fastTimer, collect, dragKey are closure-scoped singletons; arcade.js guards 'never two loops') assume a single station. maps.purpose: v7's visual layer has two independent asset systems. (1) Agent characters are real PixelLab-generated PNG frames loaded at runtime from a JSON manifest, then recolored per-agent via a CSS hue-rotate filter and downscaled — this is genuine, reusable engineering. (2) All ~50 furniture props are drawn 100% procedurally in code (sprites.js function table F); the PNGs in assets/furniture and furniture/manifest.json are NOT loaded by any runtime code and are an orphaned/alternate asset set.

keyFiles.role: The SPRITES module — the entire real character-sprite pipeline: manifest fetch+load, frame caching, per-agent hue-rotate recolor (filterFor/tintFrames), animation-state selection (drawBody/pick), foot-anchored draw. 156 lines, self-contained IIFE.
The character sprite manifest: maps logical animation-track keys ('minion.walk.south') to ordered arrays of frame PNG paths. The naming/frame convention lives here.

35 base minion PNG frames (40x40 each), one PNG per frame. Tracks: rot (4 dirs, 1 frame each), walk (4 dirs x4), drink (south x6), type (north x5), sit (4 dirs x1). This single yellow-suited base is recolored into all 16 crew.
20 Ultron PNG frames (32x45, taller — drawn ~2x via SCALE.ultron=0.85). Tracks: rot (4 dirs), walk (4 dirs x4). The boss/leader character, NOT recolored (filterFor returns '' for ULTRON).
50 furniture PNGs + furniture/manifest.json (flat key->filename map). IMPORTANT: orphaned — no runtime JS loads these. Furniture is actually drawn procedurally.

183KB. Contains procedural furniture draw-function table F[type] (drawFurn at line 3570, F defined from line 66, ~50 entries keyed by furniture 't' string), plus drawAgent (delegates to SPRITES.drawBody when ready, else drawProcedural fallback at 3622) and shared overlay rendering.
DATA.AGENTS array — each agent has id + color hex (e.g. NOVA '#4ad9ff'). DATA.AGENT[id] lookup. This color hex is the sole input to the per-agent recolor filter.

furniture[] definition array (from line 88): each item {t:type, x,y tile coords, w,h, sit/big/deco flags, pw/pwl prop-window tags}. Defines what props exist and where; keyed by 't' into both render sort and the procedural F table.
Scene compositor (line ~806): y-sorts furniture + parcels + agent bodies and draws via SPR.drawFurn / SPR.drawAgent for correct depth layering.

howItWorks: MANIFEST-DRIVEN LOADING: assets.js init() fetches assets/sprites/manifest.json (no-store). manifest.sprites is {trackKey: [path,...]}. For each key it loads every PNG via new Image()/onload (loadImage, with null-on-error tolerance) and stores surviving Images in frames[key]. Readiness gate: only sets ready=true if frames['minion.rot.south'] exists.

FRAME CONVENTION: one PNG = one frame (NOT a packed sprite sheet/atlas). File naming on disk is '<state>_<dir>[_<n>].png' (e.g. walk_south_0.png, rot_east.png, sit_north.png). The manifest re-keys these into dotted logical tracks '<set>.<state>.<dir>' (e.g. 'minion.walk.south'). Single-frame states (rot, sit) have no numeric suffix; multi-frame states (walk x4, drink x6, type x5) are zero-indexed arrays in draw order.
DIRECTIONS: four cardinal — south/north/east/west. No diagonals. East/west are distinct PNGs (not mirrored in code). Minion frames are 40x40, Ultron 32x45 (verified by IHDR).

ANIMATION STATE MACHINE (drawBody): chooses a track from body state via pick(set,names,dir) with graceful fallback (exact dir -> any dir of that name -> set.rot.south). Mapping: meeting->rot@4fps; walk->walk@10fps; working->type or sit facing north@6fps; social+sitting+hasCan->drink/sit south; sitting->sit/rot; idle->rot with a sine bob. Frame index = floor(now/(1000/fps)+phase) % frames.length, so each body's 'phase' desyncs identical agents.

PALETTE-SHIFT RECOLOR (the 1-base-to-16-crew trick): the base minion suit is bright yellow, confirmed pixel value (255,255,40) ≈ HSL hue 50, matching constants BASE_HUE=50/BASE_SAT=0.85. filterFor(agentId) converts the agent's color hex to HSL and builds a CSS canvas filter: hue-rotate(agentHue-50 deg) + saturate(s/0.85, clamped 0.1–2) + brightness(0.85+l*0.45, clamped 0.75–1.25). tintFrames applies this filter while drawImage-downscaling each frame onto a per-(agent|track) cached canvas (imageSmoothingEnabled=false for crisp nearest-neighbor). So recoloring is a GPU canvas filter over the whole sprite, not a palette LUT — cheap, cached once per agent+track. Ultron is exempt (returns '' filter, keeps native red).

SCALE: SCALE={minion:2/3, ultron:0.85}. Sprites authored at ~40px are downscaled to fit 12px tiles; Ultron downscaled less so he towers ~2x over crew. Downscale happens once at tint time and is cached.

FURNITURE (separate, procedural): render.js iterates MAP.furniture and calls SPR.drawFurn(f). drawFurn looks up F[f.t] (a draw function) and calls it with pixel rect — it draws the prop with px() primitives. The 'work' flag (an agent working within 2 tiles) is passed so props can light up. There is NO image load for furniture; the PNGs and furniture/manifest.json are dead assets.

FALLBACK: if SPRITES.ready is false (manifest/PNGs missing), drawAgent falls back to drawProcedural — a fully hand-coded pixel agent using body.color directly. So the sim renders even with zero PNG assets.
maps.realLogic: The character-sprite pipeline in assets.js is genuine, high-quality, reusable engineering: a manifest loader, an animation-track state machine with graceful fallback (pick), a real HSL-based per-agent recolor via cached canvas filters, nearest-neighbor downscale caching, and foot-anchored y-sortable drawing that returns overlay geometry. The hue-rotate recolor trick (one yellow base -> N tinted crew) is real and directly transplantable. The procedural furniture table F in sprites.js is also real, deterministic vector-pixel art (no external deps) and renders correctly today — it just doesn't use the PNGs. The drawProcedural agent fallback is a real zero-asset safety net.

PIXELLAB->MANIFEST BRIDGE: write an adapter that takes PixelLab output (4/8 directional frames + named animations like walk/drinking/picking-up + states like 'sitting down') and emits frame PNGs + a manifest.json in v7's exact '<set>.<state>.<dir>' scheme. PER-AGENT ASSET NAMESPACING: today there are two hardcoded sets (minion, ultron). For N user agents you need per-agent sprite namespaces (e.g. assets/agents/<agentId>/manifest.json + frames) so the loader can scope frames[] by agent and avoid key collisions. Generalize assets.js's single global frames{} into per-agent (or shared-base + per-agent-tint) maps.

FURNITURE AS PLACEABLE OBJECTS: the 'place a computer, agent walks to it and works' loop needs furniture to be runtime-placeable instances (not a static map.js array) with collision/sit/work-anchor metadata. Reuse the F procedural table or the PNG set, but rebuild placement as data-driven runtime state.

assets.js init() fetch('assets/sprites/manifest.json') — the seam for swapping in per-agent or PixelLab-generated manifests; make the path/agent-scoped.
sprites.js drawAgent() — already branches SPRITES.ready ? drawBody : drawProcedural. This is the clean seam: real PixelLab sprites when present, procedural fallback otherwise.

map.js furniture[] + render.js drawFurn loop — the seam where 'placed objects' (computer, desk) become things an agent can walk to and sit/work at; the work flag + pw/pwl prop-window tags are where a placed 'computer' would bind to a real agent work session / cost readout.
PixelLab MCP (create_character -> animate_character/create_character_state -> get_character download) is the runtime generation seam feeding the manifest bridge for the Terraria-style creator.
drawBody returns overlay geometry {top,w,h} — the seam where real per-agent live cost/usage badges, selection box, and status overlays attach above the sprite.
risks: The furniture PNGs are a trap: a naive 'copy the furniture sprites' will copy 50 images that the original never used. The real furniture art is CODE (procedural F table). Decide deliberately: reuse procedural code, or commit to wiring the PNGs (new loader required).

Recolor is a global hue-rotate over the WHOLE sprite, not a masked palette swap — it shifts skin/visor/can colors too, not just the suit. Fine for the stylized minion (mostly suit) but PixelLab avatars with rich multi-color palettes will recolor weirdly. For generated avatars, prefer generating the final color directly (PixelLab description/state) over hue-rotating.
4-direction-only assumption in assets.js vs PixelLab's 8-direction default — mismatch will drop diagonal frames unless reconciled.
manifest readiness gate is hardcoded to frames['minion.rot.south']; for user agents this key won't exist — the gate must be generalized or the whole pipeline silently falls back to procedural.

SCALE and frame sizes (40x40 minion, 32x45 ultron) are hardcoded; PixelLab sizes (configurable, e.g. 48px on ~68px canvas) differ and need per-avatar scale metadata or sprites render at the wrong tile size.

PixelLab generation is async (~2-5 min/character, more for animations) and costs credits/generations — the 'wake up like a baby' onboarding must mask this latency (pre-generate, or animate the recolor-base minion first, then hot-swap the real avatar when ready).

maps.subsystem: App Shell, Theming & Boot/Onboarding (v7 "StarNet" / Station OS)
maps.purpose: v7 is a no-build, zero-dependency single-page app: one index.html loads 12 plain <script> files (no modules, no bundler) that each define one global IIFE namespace (U, SFX, DATA, MAP, SPRITES, WORLD, SIM, RENDER, UI, ARCADE, PROPTERM, GAME). The shell is a CSS-grid "Station OS" dashboard wrapped in a Fallout/New-Vegas pip-boy phosphor CRT skin, fronted by a fake BIOS boot screen that gates entry on a "CLICK ANYWHERE TO TAKE COMMAND" prompt. main.js (the GAME IIFE) is the only orchestrator: it loads/inits every subsystem, runs the boot typewriter, starts the rAF loop, and handles localStorage persistence. For the new "gen" project this entire shell + theme + boot machinery is reusable as-is; only the content behind it (a pre-seeded 17-agent sim) must be replaced with a first-run agent-creation flow and a real agent backend.

keyFiles.role: The entire DOM skeleton + the ONLY dependency manifest (12 ordered <script> tags). Defines #boot overlay, #app grid (#topbar/#left/#center/#right/#bottombar), the #station <canvas>, CRT dressing divs (.crt-scan/.crt-vignette/.crt-band/.cam-hud), bottom-bar terminal buttons, and the empty #terms floating-window mount. Loads Google Fonts VT323 + css/style.css. <body class="theme-amber"> sets the default skin.

GAME IIFE = boot + game loop + persistence orchestrator. Owns settings{theme,scanlines,flicker,sound,speed}, applySettings() (sets body.className = 'theme-'+theme and toggles no-scan/no-flicker), save/load/reset to localStorage key 'starnet_save_v1', the 17-line BOOT_LINES typewriter (bootSeq), the rAF loop (sim time = 1 game-min per real sec), and start() which wires every module together in order. THE single integration seam.

743-line phosphor/CRT theming system. :root + 4 body.theme-* skins (amber/green/blue/white) each redefine ~13 --ph* CSS variables. Panel-bezel 'each panel is a small CRT monitor' box-shadow stack, h3 inverted headers, scanline/vignette/flicker via body::before/::after + @keyframes flick/band/pulse/rt-power, plus #boot styling and the .term/.pw floating-window chrome.

U namespace (rnd/clamp/money/fmtClock/esc/hash/shade) + U.bus tiny pub/sub event bus (the spine that decouples SIM↔WORLD↔UI) + SFX WebAudio synth (boot/click/open/sale/level/type bleeps). Boot audio is unlocked on first pointerdown (autoplay policy).

SPRITES IIFE: async loads assets/sprites/manifest.json, per-agent recolors ONE base 'minion' sprite via CSS hue-rotate/saturate/brightness filter derived from each agent's accent hex (filterFor), nearest-neighbor downscales+caches tinted frames, drawBody() picks walk/sit/type/drink/rot tracks. Procedural fallback if the manifest is missing. This is the avatar-recolor engine the new avatar designer can reuse.

Static content DB: DATA.MODELS (FABLE/OPUS/GPT with costMin/costMax/vendor/tag), DATA.DAILY_SUBS burn rates, DATA.ROOMS (tint/accent/desc), DATA.AGENTS array (id/room/color/harness/model/role/desc/skill/autonomy/reliability/robot). This is the exact shape the new 'create an agent' flow must PRODUCE at runtime instead of hardcoding.

UI IIFE: builds crew manifest, all bottom-bar terminal windows (SETTINGS theme picker, AGENTS dossier, TASKS, etc.), openAgent() dossier, the ULTRON chat input handler (Enter -> SIM.playerMessage), and all U.bus.on render wiring. The settings theme-swap UI and the chat-input pattern are direct precedents for onboarding.

WORLD IIFE: the room/movement/behavior system. mkBody() spawns a body at its station tile; bodies carry path[]/state/sitting/working/plan; goTo()/A*-path to props; PERS personality table; bus listeners (deliverable/flagged/intel -> physical walks). This is the 'agent walks to a computer and sits = doing work' engine the new vision reuses verbatim.

The design-DNA bible: 10 numbered design principles (movement is meaning, truthful telemetry, semantic color economy amber=production/cyan=data/red=command/green=money, diegetic terminal, etc.). The aesthetic contract the new project must preserve.
Dev launch config: npx http-server with -c-1 (no cache). Confirms the 'serve the static folder, no build step' workflow.

howItWorks: DOM LAYOUT: index.html defines two top-level siblings: #boot (full-screen z-2000 overlay) and #app (the dashboard, hidden behind boot). #app is a CSS grid (style.css:83) — grid-template-rows: 64px 1fr 44px; grid-template-columns: 232px 1fr 324px; areas 'top top top'/'left center right'/'bot bot bot'. #topbar = logo ASCII + revenue/NET/LVL stats + MANUAL/AUTOPILOT toggle + XP bar. #left = CREW MANIFEST list. #center = the <canvas id='station'> wrapped in #station-frame with CRT dressing (.crt-scan/.crt-vignette/.crt-band) and security-cam HUD overlay (.cam-hud: CAM-01, REC, FEED LIVE 60Hz). #right = stacked sections OPERATIONS FEED / MISSION CONTROL / DAILY OBJECTIVES / STATION GROUPCHAT (with the chat <input>). #bottombar = terminal-launcher buttons (data-term: settings/agents/tasks/milestones/stats/feedback/notifs) + UPLINK/save-dot/clock. #terms = empty fixed full-screen layer where floating .term / .pw windows are appended.

BOOT SEQUENCE: main.js bootSeq() (line 61) types BOOT_LINES one at a time into #boot-lines with randomized 90-200ms per-line delays ('> STARNET TERMLINK...', 'OPENCLAW GATEWAY :18789 LIVE', 'WAKING 17 AGENTS DONE', ending 'ULTRON> The station is yours.'). When typing finishes it reveals #boot-go ('▮ CLICK ANYWHERE TO TAKE COMMAND ▮', pulsing gold). A document-level click/keydown listener (start()) either FAST-FORWARDS the typewriter (if still typing) or, once done, adds #boot.off (0.6s opacity fade via CSS transition), removes the node after 700ms, fires SFX.boot()+SFX.level(), and calls the done() callback that flips running=true. The whole gate exists partly to satisfy the browser autoplay policy — the first user gesture unlocks WebAudio (pointerdown listener at main.js:130).

THEMING SYSTEM: Pure CSS-variable cascade. style.css :root defines the amber reference palette (~13 vars: --ph phosphor, --ph-bright, --ph-dim structural lines, --ph-faint recessed fills, --ink, --ph-glow/--ph-glow2 bloom, --bg, --panel/--panel2, --warn/--bad/--gold, --text, and --cam-grade a filter() color-grade applied to the canvas). Four skins (body.theme-amber/green/blue/white) each REDECLARE those vars. main.js applySettings() does the entire theme swap with one line: document.body.className = 'theme-'+settings.theme. CRT effects are global pseudo-elements: body::after = scanlines (repeating-linear-gradient), body::before = curved-glass vignette, @keyframes flick on #app = rare 7s flicker, .crt-band = rolling brightness sweep. body.no-scan / body.no-flicker classes (toggled from settings) disable them. Semantic color economy (GOALS principle 4): amber=production, cyan=data, red=command, green=money is encoded in DATA.ROOMS accents and the .pos/.neg/.gold/.warn utility classes.

MODULE WIRING (main.js start(), line 107): const had = load() (try restore from localStorage) -> if !had SIM.init() (seed fresh sim) -> applySettings() (theme/scan/flicker/sound) -> SPRITES.init() (async sprite load, procedural fallback meanwhile) -> WORLD.init() (spawn 17 bodies at station tiles, subscribe to bus events) -> RENDER.init(canvas, clickCallback) where the callback dispatches a canvas click to either UI.openAgent(agentId) or PROPTERM.open(propKey,pos) -> UI.init() (build panels, wire bottom-bar + chat input + all U.bus.on render listeners) -> bootSeq(done) where done sets running=true, starts the 1Hz UI.slowTick interval, the 30s autosave interval, and the beforeunload save. Everything after init communicates over U.bus.emit/on — SIM emits 'sale'/'chat'/'ops'/'flagged'/'deliverable'/'level'/'notify', WORLD and UI subscribe. There is NO framework; the bus is the entire architecture.

NO-BUILD ARCHITECTURE: index.html ends with 12 plain <script src> tags in strict dependency order (util -> data -> assets -> map -> sprites -> agents -> sim -> render -> ui -> arcade -> propterm -> main). No import/export, no package.json runtime deps, no transpile. Each file is one 'const NAME = (() => { ... return {publicApi} })();' IIFE that attaches a single global. The ONLY external fetches are Google Fonts (VT323) and the assets/ PNGs+manifest.json (loaded via fetch at runtime). Persistence is a single JSON blob in localStorage ('starnet_save_v1' = {sim: SIM.serialize(), settings}). Ships by opening index.html or 'npx http-server' (.claude/launch.json). GOALS.md flags the Google Fonts CDN as the one thing that breaks the offline/no-dependency promise (Loop D: 'vendor VT323 locally').
maps.realLogic: The shell, theming, boot UX, event bus, persistence, sprite-recolor pipeline, and room/movement system are all GENUINE, well-factored, reusable engineering — none of it is faked. Specifically: (1) the CSS-variable theming system + 4 skins + CRT layer is production-quality and content-agnostic; swap the variables, keep everything. (2) U.bus is a real decoupled pub/sub spine. (3) SPRITES.tintFrames/filterFor is a real, working per-agent recolor engine that turns ONE base sprite into N uniquely-colored characters via HSL-derived CSS filters — exactly the mechanism a Terraria-style avatar designer needs. (4) WORLD.mkBody/goTo + MAP.path is a real A*-pathfinding tile actor system; 'agent walks to a prop and sits = doing work' is already implemented (b.working drives the type/sit animation in assets.js drawBody). (5) save/load/reset round-trips real state. (6) The boot gate correctly solves the WebAudio autoplay-unlock problem. The data SHAPES (DATA.MODELS with per-model cost ranges, DATA.AGENTS records, DATA.ROOMS) are the correct schema for what real onboarding must generate at runtime.
maps.simulatedParts: Everything BEHIND the shell is set-dressing that must become real. The boot lines ('OPENCLAW GATEWAY :18789 LIVE', 'WAKING 17 AGENTS', model uplinks) are hardcoded theatrical strings, not real connections. DATA.AGENTS is a fixed roster of 17 pre-authored agents with invented skill/autonomy/reliability stats — there is no agent CREATION at all; the app boots straight into a populated station. The chat input (UI.init -> SIM.playerMessage) routes to a local fake-NLP parser ('ULTRON'), not a real model. Token/cost/context meters in the prop-terminal windows are procedurally generated numbers (DATA.MODELS.costMin/costMax random draws + DAILY_SUBS burn), not real billing. The 'streaming agent terminal with real tool calls' is a char-by-char fake-text engine in propterm.js. Revenue/Etsy/Fiverr economy is a self-contained simulation in sim.js. There is NO first-run flow, NO avatar designer, NO 'waking up' animation, NO purpose-giving onboarding chat, and NO real model/tool/cost integration — the persona that should emerge from onboarding (model choice, name, avatar, system-prompt/purpose) is currently just a static row in the DATA.AGENTS array.

No-build global-IIFE + strict <script> load order is simple but fragile and has no module boundaries; bolting a real async agent runtime, network calls, and a billing ledger onto globals will strain it. Consider whether the new harness stays vanilla or moves to a bundler/Electron+modules (the desktop-app target implies Electron/Tauri, which changes persistence, fetch/CORS, and the autoplay-gate assumptions).
The boot 'CLICK ANYWHERE' gate doubles as the WebAudio autoplay unlock — any onboarding flow that precedes it must preserve a real user gesture before SFX/animation audio, or sound silently fails.

Real cost/telemetry replacing faked meters means GOALS principle 2 ('truthful telemetry — screens never show set dressing') becomes a hard requirement, not a nicety; every number the UI shows must trace to a real usage value or it violates the project's own stated design contract.

DATA.AGENTS is referenced throughout (WORLD, SIM, UI, propterm) as a fixed array; converting it to a dynamic, possibly single-agent, user-created collection touches every subsystem that iterates DATA.AGENTS and assumes the 17-agent roster/rooms exist.

Avatar generation via PixelLab MCP is async, rate-limited, and credit-billed — the onboarding flow needs loading/fallback states (the existing procedural sprite fallback in assets.js is a good model), and the generated frame sizes must match the downscale/anchor assumptions in tintFrames/drawBody.

Putting a real OpenRouter/OpenClaw API key in a downloadable desktop app (per CLAUDE.md the key lives in ~/.openclaw config) is a secrets-handling risk; BYO-key and the subscription-credit proxy model must be designed so the key is never shipped in client code.

designs.area: Technical architecture for the real agent-harness desktop app (gen folder) — desktop shell, process/runtime model, agent runtime, object→tool capability mapping, persistence, and v7 reuse plan.
designs.recommendation: Build a Tauri (Rust shell) desktop app with a sidecar Node.js "agent host" process. The v7 vanilla-JS canvas world (renderer, map, movement, sprites, sound, theming, boot) is reused almost wholesale as the Tauri webview frontend. The Node sidecar owns ALL secrets, model calls, tool execution, streaming, and cost metering; it talks to the frontend over a localhost WebSocket using the SAME U.bus event vocabulary v7 already uses internally (just real events instead of SIM-faked ones). Default provider is OpenRouter (one key, all of GPT 5.5 / Opus 4.8 / Fable 5 / any slug) with BYO-key support. The load-bearing abstraction: each placeable ROOM OBJECT is a capability grant — it registers (a) a sit/work anchor in the existing map, and (b) a set of tools the seated agent may call. An agent can only call a tool while physically seated at an object that grants it, and every tool runs sandboxed (computer→Docker/WSL2 shell+code; filing cabinet→a jailed per-agent workspace dir; phone/comms→allowlisted web/email). Real streaming token usage drives b.working and the in-game cost meters, so "sitting at the computer typing" literally means "a model/tool call is in flight" and the $ counter is real billed usage.

decisions.choice: Tauri (Rust core + system WebView2) for the desktop shell, NOT Electron
decisions.rationale: Windows-first downloadable app: Tauri ships ~3-10MB installers vs Electron's ~85-150MB (no bundled Chromium — it uses the WebView2 runtime already on Win10/11). Built-in code-signed MSI/NSIS installers and a first-class auto-updater (tauri-plugin-updater with signed update manifests) cover 'downloadable + auto-update' out of the box. The v7 frontend is plain HTML/canvas/IIFE scripts with zero framework, so it drops into Tauri's webview unchanged — Tauri's webview-agnosticism is irrelevant here because we use almost no DOM APIs beyond canvas/localStorage. Lower memory footprint matters because the app also runs a Node agent host + possibly Docker.
decisions.alternatives: Electron would let the agent runtime live in its Node main process (no separate sidecar, simpler IPC) and guarantees identical Chromium rendering everywhere — but the bundle size, RAM, and update payload are poor for a consumer desktop download, and WebView2 renders this simple canvas app fine. Pure web app rejected: needs local filesystem, local Docker/shell sandbox, and secret storage. Wails/Neutralino rejected: smaller ecosystems, weaker updater/signing story.

decisions.choice: A Node.js sidecar 'agent host' process spawned by Tauri, not in-process Rust and not in the webview
decisions.rationale: The agent ecosystem (Anthropic SDK, OpenAI SDK, OpenRouter, MCP clients, the existing OpenClaw gateway the user already runs on :18789) is JS/TS-native — reusing it in Rust would mean reimplementing SDKs. Tauri ships the sidecar as a bundled binary (pkg/Node SEA) and supervises its lifecycle. Keeping agents OUT of the webview is mandatory: secrets and tool execution must never live in renderer-reachable code (the v7 risk doc explicitly flags shipping API keys in client code).
decisions.alternatives: In-process via Tauri Rust commands: forces a Rust agent loop, loses the JS SDK ecosystem and the user's existing OpenClaw/OpenRouter Node setup. Running agents in the webview: unacceptable secret exposure and no real sandbox.

decisions.choice: Frontend↔sidecar transport = localhost WebSocket carrying the existing U.bus event schema; secrets only in the sidecar
decisions.rationale: v7 is already a pure event-bus architecture (SIM emits 'deliverable'/'flagged'/'sale'/'chat'; WORLD and UI subscribe via U.bus). Replacing SIM with a WS client that re-emits real events ('agent.run.start', 'agent.tool_call', 'agent.token', 'agent.cost', 'agent.run.end', 'deliverable.ready') onto the same U.bus means WORLD/RENDER/PROPTERM need almost no change — they already react to these shapes. WebSocket (vs Tauri IPC) gives natural server→client streaming for token deltas and decouples the agent host so it could later run remotely. Keys live in OS keychain via tauri-plugin-stronghold / Windows Credential Manager, read only by the sidecar; the webview never sees them.
decisions.alternatives: Tauri invoke/emit IPC: works but couples the runtime to Tauri and is clunkier for high-rate token streaming; chosen WS keeps the runtime portable and the seam identical to v7's bus. HTTP polling: wrong for streaming. Stdin/stdout pipe to sidecar: brittle for bidirectional structured streams.

decisions.choice: OpenRouter as the default multi-model gateway, with direct-provider and BYO-key fallbacks; real metered cost from response usage
decisions.rationale: The vision explicitly wants 'GPT 5.5, Opus 4.8, Fable 5, any via OpenRouter' at character creation — one OpenRouter key unlocks all model slugs and returns normalized usage (prompt/completion/cached tokens) plus per-call cost in the response, which feeds the cost meter directly and honestly. This replaces taskCost()/estCost()'s fake U.rnd ranges. The user already runs OpenRouter locally. Direct Anthropic/OpenAI clients are kept as adapters for users who want them or for prompt-caching/streaming features OpenRouter underexposes.
decisions.alternatives: Direct-only (Anthropic+OpenAI): loses arbitrary OpenRouter slugs and forces per-vendor key management at creation. Routing through the user's existing OpenClaw gateway is supported as an adapter but not the default, since a downloadable app can't assume :18789 is running.

decisions.choice: Run-state→animation mapping driven by real streaming lifecycle, reusing v7's b.working/plan sequencer unchanged
decisions.rationale: v7 already has the exact loop: goTo(seatTile)→arrive() sits the agent, and b.working drives the type/sit sprite track. We re-point b.working from SIM.taskId to 'a real model/tool call is open'. Mapping: agent.run.start → plan a walk to the object's seat → on arrival, dispatch the real call and set sitting=true; agent.token deltas → keep working=true (and stream into the prop-terminal); agent.tool_call → set act string to the real tool name; agent.run.end → stand/clear. think() must treat an open real call like hasTask so the body doesn't wander mid-call.
decisions.alternatives: Inventing a new movement system: wasteful — v7's plan sequencer ({go/face/sit/wait/do}) is already a clean coroutine for physical errands. Cosmetic-only animation decoupled from real state: violates the 'truthful telemetry' design contract.

decisions.choice: Object→Tool capability model: a placed object is a typed capability grant gated by physical seating + sandbox
decisions.rationale: This is the product's core metaphor and its security model in one. An object instance = {type, tile, footprint, seat, facing, grants:[toolIds], sandbox}. computer→{shell.exec, code.run} in a Docker/WSL2 container scoped to that agent's workspace; filing cabinet→{fs.read, fs.write} jailed to ./workspaces/<agentId>/; phone/comms→{web.fetch, email.send} against a user-approved allowlist; easel/render→{image.generate} via PixelLab/image API. The agent runtime exposes to a model ONLY the union of tools granted by objects the agent is currently seated at. This makes capabilities literally visible/placeable (gamified) AND enforces least-privilege: no computer placed = no shell access, period. Every grant maps to a real MCP server or tool adapter in the sidecar.
decisions.alternatives: Giving every agent every tool: unsafe and breaks the placement metaphor. A flat settings checklist for permissions: less legible and not diegetic. Per-object sandbox via OS user accounts: heavier than container/dir jails for a consumer app.

decisions.choice: Persistence: SQLite (via the sidecar) for durable state; localStorage only for view/settings
decisions.rationale: Real harness state outgrows v7's single localStorage JSON blob: agent configs (model, system prompt/purpose, avatar manifest ref, granted objects), world/object placements, full transcripts, tool-call logs, a usage/credits ledger, and in-flight job records all need queryable, durable, concurrent-safe storage that survives reload of in-progress runs. SQLite in the sidecar's app-data dir is the right desktop default; the v7 save/load/serialize pattern and its lazy-migration guards become the schema-migration discipline. Generated avatar PNGs/manifests and deliverable artifacts live on disk under the app-data dir, referenced by path.
decisions.alternatives: Keep localStorage: caps out fast, no concurrency, loses in-flight jobs on reload, can't hold transcripts/artifacts. A heavier DB (Postgres) is overkill for a single-user desktop app.

decisions.choice: Decouple game-time from real-call cadence; treat runs as async jobs with concurrency/credit backpressure
decisions.rationale: v7's loop fires up to 30 game-minutes/frame and completes 'work' instantly and infallibly. Real calls are slow, failable, and cost money on error; at speed>1 the old loop would fan out many paid calls/sec. The runtime must model each run as a tracked async job (mirroring v7's reload-safe shipQueue/heraldHandoff pattern), with a concurrency cap, rate-limit handling, retry/timeout, and a credit-balance gate that replaces v7's cosmetic 5-job cap with real backpressure.
decisions.alternatives: Keep the synchronous instant-completion loop: would burn credits uncontrollably and has no failure handling. Tie call cadence to game ticks: same problem.

risks: Cost honesty is load-bearing: streaming token deltas often don't equal the final billed usage (cache reads, thinking tokens, tool-call tokens, provider rounding). The live meter must show a streaming estimate but reconcile to the provider's final usage/cost on run-end, or the 'see what it's costing you' promise erodes trust.

Sandbox escape / destructive tools: a 'computer' granting shell/code execution is the highest-risk capability. Must default to a container (Docker Desktop/WSL2) jailed to the agent's workspace with no host mount, network allowlist, and resource caps. Docker may be absent on a consumer Windows box — need a graceful 'shell unavailable until you install/enable WSL2' fallback so placing a computer doesn't silently fail or run unsandboxed.

Secret handling in a downloadable app: the OpenRouter/provider key must live in OS keychain read only by the sidecar, never in webview-reachable code or the SQLite blob. The subscription-credits proxy model (server-side key) vs BYO-key (local key) must be designed so client code never embeds a shipped key.

Runaway spend: real async paid calls + game-time fan-out can burn credits fast. Needs a hard concurrency cap, per-run/per-day budget guards, credit-balance gating before dispatch, and retry-loop limits (esp. the feedback 'retry' path) — none of which v7's free simulation needed.

Streaming cadence mismatch: model output arrives in bursty chunks and tool calls are atomic, but the prop-terminal expects ~7fps smooth char-by-char. Need a typewriter buffer that drains real tokens at a steady visual rate, decoupled from network arrival, or the feed looks janky.

Transcript growth vs the 1/sec full-rerender: v7 rebuilds window bodies via innerHTML with lines capped at 9. Real long transcripts will thrash and lose scroll/selection — streaming must append to a stable scrollback element, not rebuild it.

Dynamic single-agent roster breaks fixed-17 assumptions: WORLD/SIM/UI/propterm iterate DATA.AGENTS and assume per-id stations, rooms, buddies, and DEFS keys. First-launch single user agent will hit many null paths (beltInfo, heraldSpot, buddy, station) — needs defensive guards and runtime station/room allocation.

Runtime object placement fights v7's bake-once world: placing a computer requires updating zoneGrid/blocked/sitTiles/pwGrid AND re-baking baseCv/lightCv (no invalidate API today), plus a camera for rooms larger than the fixed 936x674 buffer (touches both render transform and toLocal hit-testing).

PixelLab avatar generation is async (~minutes) and credit-billed; the 'wake up like a baby' onboarding must mask latency (animate the recolored base minion first, hot-swap the real avatar when ready) and the global hue-rotate recolor will distort multi-color PixelLab palettes — prefer generating the final-colored avatar over hue-rotating it.

Sidecar lifecycle/ports: the Node host must be supervised (restart on crash without losing in-flight job records — hence durable jobs in SQLite), bind to a random localhost port handshaked to the webview, and shut down cleanly with the app to avoid orphaned processes holding secrets.
openQuestions: Business model fork: ship a server-side credit proxy (Hermes-style $50/mo, your OpenRouter key, you bear billing + abuse risk + need a backend service) OR BYO-API-key only (no backend, user pays provider directly, simpler/safer to ship) OR both with BYO as the launch default and credits added later? This decision drives whether you need any cloud infrastructure at all for v1.

Sandbox dependency fork: require Docker Desktop/WSL2 for the 'computer' shell/code capability (powerful but a heavy install prerequisite that will lose non-technical users) OR ship a lighter built-in sandbox (jailed Node VM / restricted subprocess, weaker isolation) OR gate shell behind an explicit 'advanced mode' and ship only safe tools (file/web/image) by default?

Single-room vs multi-room scope for v1: keep v7's fixed station layout and just make objects placeable within it (fast, reuses all baked geometry), OR build the full data-driven mutable world + camera now (matches the long-term vision but is the largest rebuild and the biggest source of risk)?

Multi-agent at launch or single-agent first: the vision starts with creating ONE agent; do agents actually collaborate/hand off work to each other (requiring inter-agent messaging, the HERALD-style ceremonies made real) in v1, or is v1 strictly one-user-agent-at-a-time with multi-agent deferred?

Deliverable destinations: are real outputs (images, code, articles) just saved to disk and shown in-game, OR do you wire real publishing/marketplace tools (Printify, Fiverr, Medium, YouTube) so the agent can actually ship — and if so, which integrations are in-scope vs aspirational set-dressing for v1?

Quality/review signal: drop v7's fake rollQuality entirely and rely solely on human (Commander) approval in the feedback gate, OR add a real LLM-judge/automated-eval that itself costs tokens and must be budgeted?

Do you keep any notion of simulated 'revenue/economy' for game feel, or fully replace the economy with credits-spent + deliverables-shipped (the honest agent-harness framing the analysis recommends)? This changes the entire right-panel/treasury UI and the core feedback loop.
