designs.area: Gamified Player Experience — onboarding, core placement loop, multi-agent growth, real cost surfacing, and the GOALS.md aesthetic mapped onto a real agent harness
designs.recommendation: Frame the whole product as "raise and run a real AI crew on a space station." Reuse v7's shell/theme/boot/recolor/movement engines verbatim and replace only the data sources. Onboarding is a 6-screen diegetic ritual (CRADLE BAY) that produces a real agent config (model id + system prompt + tools + avatar) — never a settings form, always in-fiction. The core loop is Terraria-style: a freshly-woken agent wanders an empty quarters; the user opens BUILD MODE and drops a COMPUTER prop; the agent paths to it, sits, and `b.working` is now driven by a REAL streaming model session, not SIM.taskId. Clicking the seated agent opens the prop-terminal as a live transcript with truthful token/cost/context meters sourced from real API usage. Growth is literal real-estate: earn/buy room modules, recruit more agents through the same CRADLE ritual, and the 17-agent "StarNet" station becomes the aspirational end-state of a crew the user grew one wake-up at a time. Honor GOALS.md by making every principle LITERALLY true now that the data is real: movement = a real call in flight, telemetry = real usage, the terminal = a real session.

decisions.choice: Onboarding is a diegetic 6-screen ritual ('CRADLE BAY'), not a setup wizard — model pick, avatar design, naming, wake-up animation, and purpose chat all happen in-world over the existing #boot CRT overlay layer.
decisions.rationale: GOALS principle 5 (diegetic terminal, no OS chrome) and principle 10 (fiction mirrors the real stack). The user is 'taking command', not 'configuring software'. Reuses main.js bootSeq typewriter + #boot z-2000 overlay + CRT styling wholesale; the boot click-gate already solves the WebAudio autoplay unlock that the wake-up sound needs.
decisions.alternatives: A conventional multi-step form modal — rejected: violates the no-chrome design contract and kills the emotional 'birth' beat that makes the agent feel owned.

decisions.choice: The 'give it purpose' chat is a REAL model call whose TRANSCRIPT is compiled into the agent's persisted system prompt — the onboarding conversation IS the prompt-authoring tool, surfaced as raising a newborn.
decisions.rationale: Directly satisfies the vision ('gamified onboarding configures the real agent's system prompt/role'). Reuse the #chat-input + bubble UI (ui.js:441) but repoint SIM.playerMessage at the OpenClaw gateway (localhost:18789) / OpenRouter. A lightweight 'midwife' orchestrator interviews the user, then emits a structured AgentConfig {role, goals[], tools[], constraints[], tone} that is templated into the real system prompt. The raw chat is kept as 'first memories'.
decisions.alternatives: A plain textarea 'paste your system prompt' — rejected: not gamified, and most users can't author a good prompt cold. The interview extracts it.

decisions.choice: Avatar designer offers two tracks on ONE screen: (A) INSTANT — live hue/sat/bright sliders over the recolored base minion (filterFor/tintFrames already does this, zero latency), and (B) FORGE — a PixelLab text-prompt generation that hot-swaps the real sprite in when ready. A starts selected so the agent can wake immediately.
decisions.rationale: assets.js filterFor() is a working real-time recolor engine — exposing its three filter params as sliders is near-free and gives instant Terraria-style customization. PixelLab generation is async (2-5 min) and credit-billed, so it must NOT block the wake-up; track A is the masking layer (per the risk flagged in the asset-pipeline analysis: 'animate the recolor-base minion first, then hot-swap').
decisions.alternatives: PixelLab-only — rejected: latency/cost would stall first-launch and require a network round-trip before the user sees their character. Slider-only — rejected: under-delivers on the 'DESIGN a pixel-art avatar' promise.

decisions.choice: The core loop is gated on PHYSICAL PLACEMENT: a real task can only run once a COMPUTER prop exists and the agent has walked to it and sat. No computer placed => the agent literally cannot work, only wander.
decisions.rationale: Makes 'movement is meaning' (GOALS 1) LITERAL — the sit-at-computer animation becomes the true and only visual of a real session. Reuse WORLD.goTo(seatTile)+arrive() and the {go/face/sit/do} plan sequencer (agents.js:190); generalize stations{} so a placed computer registers a sit tile + work anchor (the rebuild item already identified). Teaches the mechanic by withholding it: the empty room creates the desire to place the object.
decisions.alternatives: Auto-spawn a desk on wake — rejected: removes the player-agency placement beat that is the heart of the requested Terraria loop.

decisions.choice: b.working / f.work is rebound from SIM.taskId to a real SessionManager flag: true only while a model request or tool call is in flight, cleared on completion. The lit screen, typing arms, and CRT bloom stay cosmetic but their TRIGGER is real.
decisions.rationale: This is THE seam the rendering analysis names (agents.js:471 think(), consumed by drawBody assets.js:90 and every F.* furniture fn). Satisfies GOALS 2 (truthful telemetry — the screen lights mean a real call). Keeps the entire render/animation layer untouched.
decisions.alternatives: Keep a fake progress timer alongside real calls — rejected: reintroduces the 'decorative lie' GOALS 2 forbids and desyncs the animation from real latency.

decisions.choice: Clicking a seated agent opens the prop-terminal (PROPTERM.open) as a REAL streaming session: a typewriter buffer drains real token deltas at a steady rate, '▶ tool / ◀ result' lines are real tool_use/tool_result events, and the token/cost/context meters read real usage from the provider.
decisions.rationale: Reuses propterm.js streamHTML/feedHTML/fastTick id-targeted DOM patching and the FEED state machine; replaces only nextLine() (the named #1 seam) with a real per-agent event queue, and estCost/ctxPct with real usage. The typewriter buffer decouples smooth ~7fps visuals from bursty network arrival (the cadence risk flagged in the propterm analysis).
decisions.alternatives: A separate plain chat log window — rejected: throws away the diegetic CRT terminal that is the product's signature surface.

decisions.choice: Real per-agent cost surfaces in THREE diegetic tiers (interaction grain ratchets down, GOALS 6): (1) ambient — a small $/hr burn chip floats above a working agent's head and the topbar shows live total spend + credits remaining; (2) click — the agent dossier shows session count, tokens, real $ spent today/total, and a live cost-rate sparkline; (3) deep — the prop-terminal's TOK/COST/CTX meters tick against the actual in-flight call.
decisions.rationale: Delivers 'see how much it's costing you' as a progressive-disclosure instrument panel, matching GOALS 6 (room→agent→prop). Reuses the topbar revenue/NET slot (repurposed to SPEND/CREDITS), openAgent dossier (ui.js:226), and the propterm meters. Every number traces to a real usage value (GOALS 2 becomes a hard requirement).
decisions.alternatives: A single global billing page — rejected: not diegetic, and breaks the per-agent 'how much is THIS one costing me' framing.

decisions.choice: Growth is real-estate + recruitment: the user starts with ONE agent in ONE quarters; completing work / spending credits earns STATION XP that unlocks buyable room modules (each a placeable zone) and additional CRADLE slots. Each new agent goes through the same wake-up ritual.
decisions.rationale: Turns the static 17-agent fiction into an earned, user-grown crew (the vision's 'user-grown crew'). Reuses the XP/level/perk/milestone progression (real engine plumbing per the sim analysis) but re-points its rewards from fake economy unlocks to real capacity (room slots, agent slots, tool unlocks). The existing StarNet station becomes the visible 'end-game silhouette'.
decisions.alternatives: All rooms/agents available immediately — rejected: removes progression and the sense of building an org; also uncaps real spend with no pacing.

decisions.choice: Game-time is fully decoupled from real call cadence: the rAF loop drives only animation/wander; real model calls fire ONLY on real triggers (user directive, scheduled job, agent-initiated step), never per game-minute. Speed-up affects ambient motion, never call frequency.
decisions.rationale: Directly mitigates the top risk in the sim analysis ('at speed>1 the loop fans out many paid calls/sec — burns money uncontrollably'). The fake minuteTick generator that spawned tasks on a timer is deleted, not rebound.
decisions.alternatives: Keep the heartbeat spawning tasks at reduced rate — rejected: any time-driven auto-dispatch of paid calls is a financial footgun for a downloadable app with the user's key/credits.

decisions.choice: Drop simulated revenue entirely; the 'economy' becomes credits-spent + deliverables-shipped. Topbar NET/REV slots are repurposed to CREDITS REMAINING + WORK SHIPPED; the $50/mo subscription grants credits, with BYO-API-key as an alternate fuel source.
decisions.rationale: The sim analysis is decisive that fake sales 'structurally cannot be made real without marketplace/payment integrations' and the honest path is to meter real cost + real output. Aligns the in-game economy with the actual business model (Hermes-style credits).
decisions.alternatives: Keep simulated Etsy/Fiverr sales for game feel — rejected: violates GOALS 2 truthful-telemetry and sets a dishonest expectation in a real-money product.

risks: Wake-up latency trap: PixelLab generation (2-5 min, credit-billed) cannot block S4 IGNITION. The avatar MUST wake as the slider-recolored base minion and hot-swap when frames arrive; if the hot-swap path or readiness gate (hardcoded to 'minion.rot.south') isn't generalized per-agent, the whole pipeline silently falls back to procedural and the user's PixelLab avatar never appears.

Real cost honesty is now load-bearing (GOALS 2): streaming token deltas often don't equal the provider's final billed usage (cache reads, thinking tokens, tool tokens). The TOK/COST meters must reconcile streamed estimate with the final usage report or the 'see how much it's costing you' promise erodes trust — the exact thing the product sells.

Streaming cadence mismatch: model output arrives in bursty chunks and tool calls are atomic, but the UI assumes smooth ~7fps char-by-char typing. Without a typewriter drain buffer the live terminal looks janky; with too-deep a buffer the agent 'finishes typing' while the real call is still running, desyncing the sit animation from real latency.

Placement/bake coupling: every placed/moved object must update zoneGrid, blocked, sitTiles, AND pwGrid plus re-bake baseCv/lightCv. Miss one and agents walk through objects, no sit tile registers, or the click-to-open-terminal target is wrong. There is no invalidate/rebuild API in v7 today — it must be built deliberately.

No camera exists (fixed 936x674 buffer). A user-grown multi-room station will exceed the viewport; adding pan/zoom touches both rendering (transform before world layers) and input (toLocal must invert it) — easy to half-implement and break hit-testing.

Single-agent first-launch hits many roster null-paths: stations, buddies, HERALD/ULTRON ceremonies, belts all assume the fixed 17-agent station. The journey planners (onDeliverable/planBriefing/planVisit) need null-guards and dynamic station allocation or they crash/no-op for a lone newborn agent.

Onboarding-chat-to-system-prompt fidelity: if the ConfigCompiler mis-extracts the user's intent, the agent's real behavior won't match what the user thought they raised. The compiled prompt should be reviewable/editable at S6 COMMISSION so the gamified extraction is auditable, not a black box.

Secrets handling: a downloadable desktop app must never embed the OpenRouter/OpenClaw key in client code. BYO-key and a subscription-credit proxy must be designed so the key stays in ~/.openclaw / OS keychain, never in the shipped bundle.

abortPlan/flush double-fire: v7's flush() guarantees a side-effect fires even if a walk is interrupted (fine for fake handoffs). With real work, a cancelled walk-to-computer must NOT still mark a deliverable shipped or kick a real (paid) call — flush semantics need rethinking for real actions.
Google Fonts VT323 CDN dependency breaks the offline promise for a downloadable app (already flagged in GOALS Loop D) — vendor the font locally.
openQuestions: Fuel model at launch: subscription-credits-only ($50/mo Hermes-style), BYO-API-key-only, or both? This changes onboarding (S1 must ask for a key if BYO), the cost HUD framing (credits vs raw $), and the secrets/proxy architecture. Recommendation leans 'both, subscription default' but it's a real business fork.

When does an agent's real work actually trigger? Three models: (a) PURE PULL — agent only acts on an explicit Commander directive; (b) SCHEDULED — user sets recurring jobs (the scheduled-task MCP) that fire real calls; (c) AUTONOMOUS — agent self-initiates steps toward its purpose. (c) is the most 'alive' but the scariest for runaway spend. Which is the default, and is autonomy a per-agent toggle the user grants during onboarding?

Do we keep ANY simulated economy for game-feel, or go fully truthful (credits-spent + work-shipped only)? Dropping fake revenue is the honest/recommended path, but it removes the satisfying 'money goes up' dopamine loop — is 'deliverables shipped' + 'station grows' a strong enough reward substitute?

Multi-agent coordination: when the crew grows, do agents actually collaborate (real inter-agent message passing / a real orchestrator 'ULTRON' delegating), or is each agent an independent worker and the org structure is purely cosmetic? Real multi-agent orchestration is a large scope jump vs. reusing the HERALD/ULTRON walk choreography as flavor over independent agents.

Avatar generation default: is the PixelLab FORGE track a premium/credit-gated feature (it costs real generations) with slider-recolor as the free default, or is bespoke generation core to first-launch for everyone? Affects onboarding pacing and credit economics.

Tool grants during onboarding: should the PURPOSE interview let the user grant real tool/MCP permissions (file write, web, image gen, publish) per agent, and how is that surfaced gamified (e.g. 'equipping' the agent with tools as items)? This is where real capability — and real risk — enters.

Persistence + concurrency target: localStorage is outgrown by real transcripts/usage ledgers/artifacts. Desktop shell — Electron vs Tauri vs staying vanilla-served — determines fetch/CORS, file access, keychain, and whether the global-IIFE no-build architecture survives or needs modules. This is foundational and should be decided before the harness is built.

designs.area: Monetization, Billing & Trust/Safety layer for the "gen" desktop harness (real-agent conversion of v7/StarNet)
designs.recommendation: Launch with HYBRID billing that defaults to "Bring Your Own Key" (BYOK) — store the user's OpenRouter/Anthropic key locally and pass real metered usage through unchanged — and ship the managed-credits "Station Pass" ($50/mo grants $50 of usage at cost, app keeps a separate ~25-30% platform margin baked into a higher displayed rate) as an opt-in path behind a thin hosted proxy. BYOK gets you to market in weeks with ZERO upstream-key liability, no proxy infra, no payment/PCI exposure, and no money-transmitter/credit-balance regulatory questions; it also makes the "see how much it's costing you" promise trivially honest because you read real usage off the provider response. The credits model is the real business but it requires a hosted billing proxy + Stripe + a ledger service you do not need on day one. Crucially: BYOK and managed-credits share ONE internal cost engine and ONE in-game spend UI (repurpose v7's LEDGER/treasury_ledger window, ag.spent, estCost meters, TOP BURNERS, DAILY LEDGER) — only the *source of the dollar number* and *who holds the upstream key* differ, so shipping BYOK first costs nothing toward the credits build. Gate all real tool execution (shell/files/web) behind the EXISTING object-placement mechanic as the capability surface: an agent can only do what the room contains — placing a "computer" grants compute, a "terminal/console" prop grants shell, a "filing cabinet" grants disk, an "uplink/web" prop grants network — turning v7's set-dressing into a literal, legible permission system.

decisions.choice: Ship BYOK-first, credits-second (hybrid), not credits-first or pure-BYOK-forever
decisions.rationale: Pure BYOK can ship in weeks with no proxy, no Stripe, no upstream-key custody, no balance/escrow regulatory exposure, and makes truthful telemetry (GOALS principle 2) trivial since usage comes straight off the provider response. But BYOK alone leaves the $50/mo Hermes-style revenue on the table and asks non-technical users to obtain an API key. Hybrid keeps the fast launch AND keeps the managed-credits business as a flip-the-switch upgrade because both paths feed ONE cost engine and ONE spend UI.
decisions.alternatives: Credits-first (blocked on proxy+Stripe+ledger+key custody+possible money-transmitter analysis before any launch); pure BYOK forever (no recurring revenue, high signup friction, no margin).

decisions.choice: For managed credits, route ALL model traffic through a thin hosted proxy (gen-gateway) that holds the upstream keys; the desktop app NEVER ships an upstream key
decisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md already flags shipping the OpenRouter key in client code as a secrets risk. A desktop binary is fully inspectable, so any embedded key is immediately extractable and abusable. The proxy holds platform keys server-side, authenticates the app with a per-account short-lived token, meters tokens, applies markup, decrements the credit ledger, and streams the response back. This is the same pattern the local OpenClaw gateway (:18789) already proves out — repoint the runtime from localhost:18789 to the hosted gateway for credits-mode, keep :18789 for local/BYOK power users.
decisions.alternatives: Embed a platform key in the app (immediately extractable, unbounded liability); per-user provisioned upstream keys (provider ToS issues, no central metering/markup, hard to revoke).

decisions.choice: Display real $ at a marked-up rate in credits-mode, real $ at provider-cost in BYOK-mode, from one cost engine
decisions.rationale: The credit price = upstream cost x (1 + margin). To keep the in-game meter honest AND profitable, the gateway returns the *billed credit amount* (already marked up) as the authoritative number; the app shows that. In BYOK mode the same engine shows raw provider cost (markup=0). One CostEngine.price(usage, rateCard) function with a per-mode rate card means the LEDGER UI, ag.spent, and estCost are identical code in both modes.
decisions.alternatives: Two separate cost paths (drift, double-maintenance, risk of showing a number that doesn't match the bill — directly violates the truthful-telemetry design contract).

decisions.choice: Decouple in-game time from real call cadence; meter on real usage events, not the sim minute-tick
decisions.rationale: v7's loop fires up to 30 game-minutes/frame and at speed>1 would fan out many paid calls/second, burning credits uncontrollably (flagged in the sim subsystem risks). Real billing must be driven by actual streaming usage events (token deltas + final usage report), reconciled to the final provider usage number, NOT by t.prog/t.dur. The sit-at-computer animation starts on real call-begin and ends on real call-return.
decisions.alternatives: Keep sim-clock-driven cost (mints fake numbers, decouples spend from reality, runs up real bills at high sim speed).

decisions.choice: Reconcile streaming token estimates against the FINAL provider usage report before committing to the ledger
decisions.rationale: Streaming token deltas often do not equal the final billed usage (cache reads, thinking tokens, tool-call tokens) — flagged in the propterm subsystem risk. Show a live *estimate* during streaming (estCost-style), then on call completion overwrite ag.spent with the authoritative usage*rate from the provider/proxy response so the committed ledger never drifts from the real bill.
decisions.alternatives: Trust streaming deltas only (meter subtly wrong, erodes trust); only show cost at the end (loses the live 'watch it cost you' drama that is the product hook).

decisions.choice: Make object placement the capability/permission surface; no ambient tool access
decisions.rationale: Real agents executing shell/files/web on the user's machine is the single biggest risk. v7 already has the perfect legible metaphor: an agent can only act through props in its room. Reify it — a placed 'computer' = model compute; 'terminal/console' prop = shell tool (scoped to a sandbox dir); 'filing cabinet' = filesystem read/write (scoped); 'uplink/satellite' prop = network/web. Removing the object revokes the capability. This is both UX and security: the room IS the allow-list, and it's visible.
decisions.alternatives: Global tool permissions in a settings menu (invisible, easy to over-grant, no in-world meaning); always-on tools (unacceptable risk on a user's machine).

decisions.choice: Default-deny tool execution with per-action permission prompts + a sandboxed working directory; agents cannot touch arbitrary paths
decisions.rationale: Even with object-gating, the FIRST time an agent in a session wants to run a shell command, write a file, or hit a domain, prompt the user (allow once / allow for session / always allow this agent+capability / deny), and confine file/shell ops to a per-agent workspace directory by default. Note CLAUDE.md says bypassPermissions is set for THIS dev instance — that must NOT carry into the shipped product; shipped default is prompt-on-first-use.
decisions.alternatives: Trust the agent (catastrophic on a real machine); allowlist-only with no prompts (too rigid, users hit walls); inherit the dev bypassPermissions default (ships a footgun).

decisions.choice: Repurpose v7's LEDGER agent + treasury_ledger (TRS-01) window + ag.spent/estCost/TOP BURNERS/DAILY LEDGER as the real billing dashboard
decisions.rationale: These surfaces already exist and already render per-agent BURNED (ag.spent), an estCost meter, a sorted TOP BURNERS list, and a DAILY LEDGER history (confirmed in data.js:80 LEDGER agent, propterm.js:799 BURNED, :1236 treasury_ledger, :1273 TOP BURNERS). Swap their data source from taskCost()/DATA.DAILY_SUBS RNG to the real CostEngine and they become the production billing UI with near-zero new UI code. Add a CREDITS REMAINING gauge and a low-balance warning to the topbar (which already shows revenue/NET).
decisions.alternatives: Build a new billing UI from scratch (wasteful — the diegetic CRT ledger is a product differentiator and already built).

decisions.choice: Distribute as a code-signed Windows installer (NSIS/MSI via Electron-builder or Tauri) with auto-update; accounts only required for credits-mode
decisions.rationale: Desktop-app target implies Electron or Tauri (flagged in app-shell risks). Tauri gives a smaller, more secure binary (Rust core, system webview) which suits a security-sensitive agent harness; Electron is faster to port the vanilla-JS shell verbatim. Either way: an EV/OV code-signing cert avoids SmartScreen scares, and a signed auto-update channel (Squirrel/Tauri updater) is mandatory for shipping security fixes to a tool that runs real code. BYOK-mode needs no account (key is local); credits-mode requires a lightweight account tied to Stripe.
decisions.alternatives: Unsigned zip (SmartScreen blocks, no trust, no auto-update — unacceptable for a tool that runs shell on user machines); web app (can't do local shell/files, defeats the vision).

decisions.choice: Vendor fonts/assets locally and treat the app as offline-capable except for model/proxy calls
decisions.rationale: GOALS.md already flags the Google Fonts VT323 CDN as breaking the offline/no-dependency promise; a downloadable app must bundle it. Transcripts and state stay local by default (privacy posture below).
decisions.alternatives: Keep CDN font (breaks offline, leaks a request, fails in air-gapped use).

risks: Embedding any upstream provider key in the downloadable binary = immediate extraction and abuse; the credits-mode proxy MUST hold keys server-side and the app must only ever carry a revocable per-account token (CLAUDE.md already flagged this).

Real metered cost is spikier and can be far higher than v7's friendly invented ranges (GPT 0.14-0.42/task). The $50/mo credit unit economics, objectives, and perks are tuned to fake numbers and need re-tuning against real spend, or a single heavy Opus/thinking session blows a month's credits in minutes.

Runaway spend at high sim speed: the v7 loop can fan out many paid calls/second. Without decoupling game-time from real call cadence + a hard balance stop + a per-minute/-session spend cap, users (or a buggy loop) can burn real money uncontrollably.

Money-transmitter / stored-value regulatory exposure: selling prepaid 'credits' redeemable for a service can trigger gift-card/stored-value rules depending on jurisdiction, rollover, and refundability. Keep credits non-refundable, non-cash, single-purpose, expiring; get legal review before scaling the credits tier. (BYOK launch sidesteps this entirely.)

Real agents running shell/file/web on a user's machine is the dominant safety risk: prompt-injection in fetched web content or a deliverable could drive destructive shell/file actions. Object-gating + default-deny prompts + sandboxed workspace dir + domain allow-list are mandatory, not optional. The dev bypassPermissions setting must never ship.

Truthful-telemetry is now a hard contract (GOALS principle 2): every number shown must trace to a real usage value. Streaming token deltas != final billed usage (cache/thinking/tool tokens) — must reconcile to the provider's final usage report or the meter is subtly wrong and erodes the core trust promise.

Markup transparency / ToS: charging more than raw provider cost in credits-mode must be disclosed (it's a managed service, not pass-through). Some provider ToS restrict reselling/proxying API access — verify OpenRouter/Anthropic terms permit a metered reseller proxy before launching credits-mode.

Transcript privacy: agent transcripts can contain user secrets, file contents, and PII. Default must be local-only with explicit opt-in before anything leaves the device; redact secrets from logs; clear ToS/privacy policy required before any cloud sync or telemetry.

Top-up/refund abuse and chargebacks on Stripe; credit-balance accounting must be atomic server-side (decrement before/at dispatch) to prevent overspend races, especially with concurrent agents sharing one balance.

Code-signing + auto-update is security-critical for a tool that executes code: an unsigned or hijackable update channel is a supply-chain attack vector. EV/OV cert + signed update manifests are required day one.

MARGIN & PRICING: For the $50/mo Station Pass, does $50 grant exactly $50 of usage at COST (margin comes only from breakage/unused credits, Hermes-style) or $50 grants ~$38 of usage at a 25-30% markup (margin on every call)? These imply very different unit economics and different honesty framing in the in-game meter.

CREDIT POLICY: Do monthly credits roll over or expire? Are top-ups refundable? (Expiring, non-refundable, single-purpose credits materially reduce stored-value/money-transmitter exposure — but hurt user goodwill.)

ELECTRON vs TAURI: Port the vanilla-JS shell verbatim into Electron (fastest, larger/less-sandboxed binary) or rebuild the shell in Tauri (smaller, Rust core, better security posture for a tool that runs real shell/files)? This affects timeline, binary size, and the safety story.

TOOL CAPABILITY SCOPE AT LAUNCH: Which real tools ship in v1 — model calls + image gen only (lowest risk), or also shell/filesystem/web (high value, high risk)? Object-gating supports a staged rollout (computer-only first, terminal/cabinet/uplink later).

SANDBOX STRICTNESS: Confine agent shell/file ops to a per-agent workspace directory only (safest, but limits 'do real work on my computer'), or allow broader access behind per-action prompts (more powerful, more dangerous)? Where is the line for v1?
WHO BEARS FAILED-CALL COST: In credits-mode, do users pay for calls that error/timeout/refuse (provider still bills tokens), or does the platform absorb retries? This affects both trust and margin.
MAC/LINUX: Windows-only at launch (matches the user's environment and current vision) or cross-platform from day one? Affects signing/notarization and sandbox implementation effort.

ORCHESTRATOR MODEL COST: The 'ULTRON' orchestrator that parses directives and configures agent purpose is itself a billed model call. Is orchestrator usage charged to the user's credits, bundled into the subscription base, or run on a cheaper fixed model to control cost?

# StarNet → Real: Build Plan for the Gamified AI-Agent Harness (`gen/`)

**Document owner:** Lead Planner · **Date:** 2026-06-13 · **Status:** Decision document, ready to execute against.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

The product is a downloadable Windows desktop app that turns a pixel-art space station into a living dashboard for **real** AI agents: you create an agent like a Terraria character (pick a model, design a pixel avatar, name it), raise it through a gamified onboarding chat that writes its real system prompt, then watch it walk around a room and sit down at objects you place — and when it sits at a computer it is genuinely running a model, calling real tools, and spending real money you can watch tick up. Every number on screen is truthful: the typing animation means a model call is in flight, the cost meter reads real provider usage, and the deliverables are real files written to disk. Agents can only do what the room physically contains — placing a "computer" grants compute, a "terminal" grants shell, a "filing cabinet" grants disk — so the room layout *is* the permission system, visible and legible. The business model is a Hermes-style $50/mo credit subscription with Bring-Your-Own-Key as the launch default, surfaced in-game as a per-agent spend meter and a station-wide credit gauge.

**The single biggest technical bet:** that we can keep v7's entire vanilla-JS canvas world (renderer, tile map, movement/sit/work state machine, sprite recolor, prop-terminal, CRT theme) essentially **unchanged** as the frontend, and make it real solely by **replacing the fake `SIM` module with a thin event adapter that re-emits real agent-runtime events onto the exact same `U.bus` event vocabulary the frontend already listens for.** If that seam holds, we ship the look-and-feel of v7 with real agents behind it; if it doesn't, the rebuild balloons. Everything below is structured to validate that bet as early as Phase 1.

---

## 2. What We Keep From v7 vs What Is Genuinely New

### Keep — reused near-verbatim (the engine)

- **Provider adapters** — OpenRouter (default), direct Anthropic/OpenAI, local OpenClaw gateway.
- **Capability/tool registry + sandbox** — object→tool mapping, per-action permission prompts, jailed workspace dirs.
- **Cost & credits ledger** — real metered usage, reconciliation, subscription/BYOK fuel.

**Why Tauri:** ~3–10 MB installers vs Electron's ~85–150 MB (uses the WebView2 runtime already on Win10/11); first-class signed installer + auto-updater; the v7 frontend is plain canvas/IIFE with almost no DOM dependency, so it drops into the webview unchanged; lower RAM matters because we also run a Node host and possibly Docker.

**Why a Node sidecar (not Rust, not webview):** the entire agent ecosystem (Anthropic/OpenAI SDKs, OpenRouter, MCP clients, the user's existing OpenClaw setup) is JS/TS-native — reimplementing in Rust is wasted effort. Agents must live **outside** the webview because secrets and tool execution can never be renderer-reachable.

**Why WS carrying `U.bus` events:** v7 is already a pure event-bus architecture. If the bridge re-emits real events under the same names the frontend already subscribes to, WORLD/RENDER/PROPTERM need almost no change. WS (vs Tauri IPC) is natural for server→client token streaming and keeps the host portable.

**Why OpenRouter default:** the vision explicitly wants "GPT 5.5, Opus 4.8, Fable 5, any via OpenRouter." One key unlocks all slugs and returns normalized usage + per-call cost, which feeds the meter honestly. The user already runs OpenRouter locally.

> **Model-id note:** the in-fiction model names ("Opus 4.8", "Fable 5", "GPT 5.5") must map to **real, current** provider slugs at build time — do not hardcode the v7 fake `DATA.MODELS` ids. Resolve live model ids and per-token pricing from the provider (OpenRouter `/models`) at runtime into the `RateCard`. When wiring the Anthropic/Claude adapter specifically, verify current model ids, pricing, streaming-usage fields, and tool-use format against the live Claude API reference rather than memory.

## 4. The Core Abstraction: Room Objects → Agent Capabilities/Tools

A placed object is a **typed capability grant** and a **security boundary** in one. This is the product's central metaphor *and* its least-privilege model: an agent can call a tool **only while physically seated at an object that grants it**. No computer placed → no compute, period. Remove the object → revoke the capability. The room is the visible allow-list.

**Object schema** (runtime, replaces v7's static `furniture[]` literals):
```
ObjectInstance {
  id, type, tile{x,y}, footprint{w,h}, rot,
  seat?{tile,facing}, workAnchor?{tile,facing},
  grants:[toolId], sandbox{kind, scope}, spriteKey, ownerAgentId?
}
```

### Starter object → tool table

| Object (sprite) | Grants (real tools) | Sandbox / scope | Safety gate | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Computer / workstation** (`pixelrig`,`desk2`) | `model.chat` (run the agent's LLM), `agent.think` | Model call only — no host access | Always-on once seated; this is the baseline "is working" object | **P1** |
| **Terminal / console** (`desk`,`console`) | `shell.exec`, `code.run` | Docker/WSL2 container **or** restricted subprocess, jailed to `workspaces/<agentId>/`, no host mount, network allowlist, CPU/mem caps | Default-deny **per-action prompt** (allow once / session / always this agent / deny) | **P3** |
| **Filing cabinet** (`cabinet`) | `fs.read`, `fs.write`, `fs.list` | Confined to `workspaces/<agentId>/` only | Prompt on first write per session; reads within jail auto-allowed | **P3** |
| **Uplink / satellite dish** (`dish`) | `web.fetch`, `web.search` | Domain **allowlist**; no localhost/private-IP ranges | Prompt per new domain; treat fetched content as untrusted (prompt-injection surface) | **P3** |
| **Easel / render station** (`holotable`) | `image.generate` (PixelLab/image API) | API call; output written to jailed workspace | Cost-gated (counts against credits); no host access | **P3** |
| **Comms desk** (`djbooth`→repurpose) | `email.send`, `message.post` | Allowlisted recipients/endpoints only | Explicit per-recipient confirm; off by default | **P4 / aspirational** |
| **Mailbox / outbox** (`belt`) | `deliverable.publish` (save to disk + show in-game) | Local disk only by default | None for local save; publishing to external services (Printify/Medium/etc.) is **out of scope for v1** | **P3** |

**Non-negotiable safety defaults (shipped builds):**
- **Default-deny.** The dev `bypassPermissions: true` in `~/CLAUDE.md` is for *this* dev instance only and must **never** ship. Shipped default is prompt-on-first-use per capability.
- **Sandboxed workspace.** All shell/file ops confined to a per-agent directory; no arbitrary-path access without explicit escalation.
- **Object-gated tool set.** The agent runtime exposes to the model **only** the union of tools granted by objects the agent is currently seated at — enforced in the sidecar before any tool dispatch, not in the renderer.
- **Untrusted content.** Web-fetched content and deliverables are treated as prompt-injection vectors; they cannot silently widen capability.

A `ConfigCompiler` turns the transcript into a structured `AgentConfig {role, goals[], allowedTools[], constraints[], tone}` and templates it into the **real system prompt**. ### The core loop (post-onboarding)

1. The new agent **wanders aimlessly** in an empty room — it has no computer, so it *literally cannot work*. This withholding is the tutorial: the empty room creates the desire to place an object.
2. The user opens **BUILD MODE**, drags a **COMPUTER** from the inventory tray, sees a ghost preview snapped to the tile grid with green/red validity (`walkable` + footprint-free), and places it. 3. The user gives a **directive** (chat) or the agent has a scheduled job. A real task is dispatched.
4. The agent **paths to the computer, sits, and `b.working` flips true** — driven by a real model call in flight.
5. The user **clicks the agent** → the prop-terminal opens as a live session (real streamed tokens, real tool lines, real cost). Ambient $/hr chip floats over the agent's head; topbar shows live spend + credits remaining.
6. **Growth:** shipped work / credits spent earn Station XP → unlock buyable room modules and additional Cradle slots → recruit more agents through the same ritual. The full 17-agent StarNet station is the **ghosted "destiny" silhouette** the crew grows into.

## 6. How a Real Agent Run Maps to Movement + Live Terminal + Cost

This is the heart of "truthful telemetry" — every visual is bound to a real event.

```
USER DIRECTIVE / SCHEDULED JOB
   │  (game-time is DECOUPLED: real calls fire ONLY on real triggers, never per game-minute)
   ▼
host: SessionManager.dispatch(agentId, task)  ── creates durable RunJob (reload-safe)
   │
   ├─► WS: agent.run.start ──► U.bus.emit('agent.run.start')
   │        WORLD: plan a walk to the computer's workAnchor  →  goTo(seatTile)
   │
   ├─ agent arrives & sits ──► WORLD.arrive(): state='work', sitting=true
   │        (think() now PINS the body at the desk while a real call is open —
   │         treats an open call exactly like the old hasTask, so it never wanders mid-call)
   │
   ├─► model call opens ──► b.working = SessionManager.hasOpenCall(agentId)  [was !!SIM.taskId]
   │        drawBody picks the 'type'/'sit' track facing north; CRT screen lights (f.work)
   │        — the typing animation now LITERALLY means "a model call is in flight"
   │
   ├─► streaming tokens ──► agent.token deltas
   │        PROPTERM: a TYPEWRITER BUFFER drains real tokens at a steady ~7fps visual rate
   │        (decouples smooth typing from bursty network arrival); appends to a STABLE
   │        scrollback element (not the 1Hz innerHTML rebuild) so long transcripts don't thrash
   │
   ├─► tool_use start/result ──► agent.tool_call
   │        PROPTERM: real '▶ shell.exec {...}' / '◀ exit 0 (1.2s)' lines (was random pools)
   │        WORLD: act string = the real tool name (was authored narration)
   │
   ├─► usage deltas ──► agent.cost (LIVE ESTIMATE)
   │        CostEngine.price(usage, rateCard) → live $ estimate
   │        PROPTERM meters #ft (TOK)=real tokens, #fm (COST)=real $, #fx (CTX)=real ctx-used/window
   │        (replaces st.tok counter, estCost interpolation, ctxPct formula)
   │
   └─► agent.run.end ──► RECONCILE: overwrite ag.spent with provider's FINAL usage*rate
            (streaming deltas ≠ final billed usage — cache/thinking/tool tokens — so the
             committed ledger is the authoritative number, never the streamed estimate)
            WORLD: stand, clear act; deliverable written to disk, artifact ref stored
            CostHUD: decrement credits; topbar spend updates; dossier sparkline ticks
```

**The four named seams being rebound** (from the analyses):
- `agents.js:471` `hasTask = !!ag.taskId` → `SessionManager.hasOpenCall(agentId)`.
- `propterm.js` `nextLine()` (the #1 streaming seam) → consume a real per-agent event queue.
- `propterm.js` `estCost`/`ctxPct`/`st.tok` → real usage from the provider.
- `sim.js` `taskCost()`/`DATA.DAILY_SUBS` → `CostEngine` + `RateCard`.

## 7. Monetization & Safety Summary

**Billing — ship BYOK-first, credits-second (hybrid).** Both paths feed **one `CostEngine` and one in-game spend UI**; only the *source of the dollar number* and *who holds the upstream key* differ, so shipping BYOK first costs nothing toward the credits build.

- **BYOK (launch default):** user's OpenRouter/Anthropic key stored in OS keychain locally, real usage read straight off the provider response (markup = 0). Ships in weeks: zero proxy infra, zero upstream-key custody, zero payment/PCI/money-transmitter exposure. Makes "see how much it's costing you" trivially honest.
- **Credits ("Station Pass", $50/mo, opt-in):** all traffic routed through a thin hosted **gen-gateway** proxy that holds upstream keys server-side, authenticates the app with a short-lived per-account token, meters tokens, applies markup, decrements the ledger atomically, and streams back. **The desktop app never ships an upstream key.** Stripe-backed; credits non-refundable / non-cash / single-purpose / expiring to minimize stored-value regulatory exposure.
- **Cost honesty:** show a live streaming *estimate*, then **reconcile to the provider's final usage report** before committing to the ledger.

**Repurpose v7's existing billing surfaces** — `LEDGER` agent, `treasury_ledger` window, `BURNED` (`ag.spent`), `TOP BURNERS`, `DAILY LEDGER` — by swapping their data source from RNG to the real `CostEngine`. Add a **CREDITS REMAINING** gauge + low-balance warning to the topbar (repurposing the revenue/NET slot). Drop simulated revenue entirely: the economy becomes **credits-spent + deliverables-shipped**.

**Safety (mandatory, not optional):** object-gated capabilities + default-deny per-action prompts + sandboxed per-agent workspace + domain allowlist. Hard **spend backpressure** (concurrency cap, per-run/per-day budget guard, credit-balance gate before dispatch, retry-loop limit) replaces v7's cosmetic 5-job cap. Code-signed binary + signed auto-update channel are security-critical for a tool that executes real code. Transcripts local-only by default; explicit opt-in before anything leaves the device; secrets redacted from logs. Vendor the VT323 font locally (the CDN dependency breaks the offline promise).

## 8. Phased Roadmap

Each phase lists **deliverables**, **v7 files to port**, and a **definition of done (DoD)**. Phases are ordered to validate the central bet (Section 1) as early as possible — Phase 1 proves a real agent run drives the reused world before any onboarding or billing work.

### Phase 0 — Scaffold + reuse the v7 engine
**Goal:** the v7 station runs inside a Tauri webview talking to a Node sidecar over WS, still visually identical, with the fake `SIM` swapped for a stub adapter.
- **Deliverables:** Tauri project + WebView2 host; Node sidecar spawned/supervised by Tauri; localhost WS handshake (random port); v7 frontend dropped in unchanged; `SIM` replaced by a **stub WS bridge** that re-emits canned events onto `U.bus` (proves the seam); VT323 vendored locally; SQLite initialized in app-data dir.
- **Port from v7:** `util.js`, `map.js`, `agents.js`, `render.js`, `assets.js`, `sprites.js`, `ui.js`, `propterm.js`, `css/style.css`, `index.html`, `assets/sprites/*` — all near-verbatim. Replace only `sim.js` + `main.js` boot wiring.
- **DoD:** app launches as a signed-dev build, the station renders and animates, an agent walks/sits when the stub bridge emits a fake `agent.run.start`, and the webview never imports a secret. The "swap SIM for an event adapter" bet is demonstrated end-to-end with stub data.

### Phase 1 — One real agent, one room, one working computer, real streaming + cost
**Goal:** prove the whole truthful-telemetry chain with a single hardcoded agent and a single placed computer. **This is the make-or-break phase.**
- **Deliverables:** `SessionManager` runs a real OpenRouter model call for one agent on a user directive; `agent.run.start/.token/.tool_call/.cost/.run.end` flow over WS; `b.working` rebound to `hasOpenCall`; PROPTERM shows real streamed tokens via a **typewriter buffer** into a **stable scrollback**; real **TOK/COST/CTX** meters with **final-usage reconciliation**; one runtime-placeable COMPUTER object with incremental grid updates + re-bake; `CostEngine` + `RateCard` (BYOK, markup 0); durable `RunJob`; spend/concurrency backpressure; **game-time decoupled** (the `minuteTick` task generator is deleted, not rebound).
- **Port from v7:** `propterm.js` (`streamHTML`/`feedHTML`/`fastTick`, replace `nextLine`/`estCost`/`ctxPct`); `agents.js` (`goTo`/`arrive`, rebind `think()` `hasTask`); the `F.pixelrig`/`desk2` furniture art; `ui.js` `openAgent` dossier + `LEDGER`/`treasury_ledger` surfaces.
- **DoD:** the user types a directive, a single agent walks to a placed computer, sits, and a **real Opus/GPT call streams into the terminal** while a **real $ meter** climbs and reconciles to the provider's final bill on completion; a real deliverable file is written to disk and referenced. No fake numbers anywhere in the chain.

### Phase 2 — Onboarding / character creator
**Goal:** the user creates their first agent in-fiction; agents are dynamic, not a hardcoded roster.
- **Deliverables:** Cradle Bay S1–S6; live avatar recolor sliders; PixelLab FORGE track with hot-swap + generalized readiness gate (per-agent, not hardcoded `minion.rot.south`); `ConfigCompiler` (interview → editable real system prompt); first-run gate (no agent → onboarding, else boot); dynamic single-agent roster with **null-guards** for missing buddies/rooms/stations/belts (the journey planners assume the 17-agent station).
- **Port from v7:** `main.js` `#boot`/`bootSeq`; `assets.js` `filterFor`/`tintFrames`/`drawBody`; `ui.js` chat input; `@keyframes rt-power`.
- **DoD:** a brand-new user lands in Cradle Bay, picks a model, designs an avatar, names it, watches it wake, gives it purpose via real chat, edits the compiled prompt, and it drops into a room — then Phase-1's loop works for that user-created agent.

### Phase 3 — Object → tool expansion + multi-agent
**Goal:** the room becomes a real capability surface; multiple agents coexist.
- **Deliverables:** full BuildMode + inventory tray (place/move/pick-up, ghost preview, validity); `CapabilityManager` (object→tool grants, seated-only enforcement); `PermissionBroker` + sandbox (terminal→jailed shell, cabinet→jailed fs, uplink→allowlisted web, easel→image gen); **camera** (pan/zoom; `toLocal` inverts the transform); StationGrowth (XP→room modules + Cradle slots); multiple concurrent agents with per-agent session keying; reconciled flush semantics (a cancelled walk must **not** fire a real paid action or mark a deliverable shipped).

## 10. Top Risks + Consolidated Open Product Decisions

### Top risks (with the mitigation already baked into the plan)
1. **Cost honesty is load-bearing** — streamed token deltas ≠ final billed usage (cache/thinking/tool tokens). *Mitigation:* live estimate during stream, reconcile to provider final before committing (Section 6).
2. **Sandbox escape / destructive tools** — a "terminal" granting shell is the highest-risk capability; Docker may be absent on consumer Windows. *Mitigation:* default-deny prompts + jailed workspace + allowlist; graceful "shell unavailable until WSL2 enabled" fallback so placing the object never silently runs unsandboxed.
3. **Runaway spend** — real async paid calls + game-time fan-out can burn credits fast. *Mitigation:* game-time fully decoupled from call cadence; hard concurrency/budget/balance gates; retry-loop limits.
4. **Secrets in a downloadable binary** — any embedded upstream key is extractable. *Mitigation:* BYOK key in OS keychain read only by sidecar; credits-mode keys server-side behind the proxy; never in client code or the save blob.
5. **Placement fights v7's bake-once world + no camera** — placing objects requires incremental `zoneGrid`/`blocked`/`sitTiles`/`pwGrid` updates + re-bake (no invalidate API today), and rooms can exceed the fixed 936×674 buffer. *Mitigation:* build the mutable-world API + camera in P1/P3 deliberately.
6. **Single-agent breaks fixed-17 assumptions** — stations/buddies/HERALD ceremonies/belts assume the full roster. *Mitigation:* null-guards + dynamic station allocation in P2.
7. **Streaming cadence + transcript growth** — bursty network vs smooth ~7fps typing; 1Hz innerHTML rebuild thrashes long transcripts. *Mitigation:* typewriter drain buffer + stable append-only scrollback (P1).
8. **PixelLab latency/palette** — async ~minutes, credit-billed; global hue-rotate distorts multi-color palettes. *Mitigation:* wake as recolored minion, hot-swap later; prefer generating final-colored avatars over hue-rotating.
9. **Regulatory (credits)** — prepaid stored-value can trigger money-transmitter rules. *Mitigation:* BYOK launch sidesteps it; credits non-refundable/non-cash/single-purpose/expiring; legal review before scaling.
10. **Code-signing / update channel** — an unsigned or hijackable updater is a supply-chain attack vector for a tool that runs real code. *Mitigation:* EV/OV cert + signed update manifests from day one of distribution.

| **D2** | **Credit margin model:** $50 = $50-at-cost (margin from breakage) or $50 = ~$38-at-markup (~25–30% on every call)? | **Markup on every call**, disclosed in-app. Sustainable; breakage-only is fragile. | Unit economics + in-game meter framing. |
| **D3** | **Credit policy:** rollover? refundable? | **Expire monthly, non-refundable, single-purpose.** Minimizes stored-value exposure. | Legal posture; UX goodwill tradeoff. |
| **D4** | **When does an agent actually run?** Pure-pull (directive only) / scheduled / autonomous self-initiation? | **Pull as the default; scheduled as opt-in; autonomy a per-agent toggle granted at onboarding.** Autonomy is the scariest for spend. | Trigger model in `SessionManager` (P1/P3). |
| **D5** | **Tool scope at v1:** model+image only, or also shell/fs/web? | **Computer (model) only in P1; terminal/cabinet/uplink in P3 behind prompts.** Staged by object placement. | Sandbox effort; safety surface. |

| **D7** | **Multi-agent coordination:** real inter-agent messaging/orchestration, or independent workers with cosmetic org? | **Independent workers in v1; HERALD/ULTRON walk-choreography as flavor.** Real orchestration is a large scope jump — defer. | P3 scope. |
| **D8** | **Single-room vs multi-room for v1:** reuse fixed station + placeable objects, or full data-driven world + camera now? | **Placeable objects in the existing room for P1; camera + room modules in P3.** | P1 vs P3 size. |
| **D9** | **Deliverable destinations:** disk-only, or wire real publishing (Printify/Fiverr/Medium/YouTube)? | **Disk-only + show in-game for v1.** External publishing is aspirational set-dressing — out of scope. | P3 tool list. |
| **D10** | **Quality/review signal:** human approval only, or add a real LLM-judge eval? | **Human (Commander) approval only for v1.** An eval itself costs tokens — defer. | Feedback-gate behavior. |
